summary: I independently verified every finding against the live code and ran the suite. The factual backbone of the audit is solid and reproducible: `cargo test` passes exactly 19 tests across exactly 4 of 14 backend modules — text_cleanup (6), trial (8), license (3), activation (2) — confirmed by both a test-attribute count and a clean run. The frontend has no test runner (no vitest/jest/testing-library in package.json devDependencies; no .test.* files), and `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` is the only workflow: it triggers solely on `push: tags: v*` / `workflow_dispatch`, runs on macos-14 only, and never invokes cargo test, clippy, fmt, or npm lint — so the green tests are advisory and there is NO Windows job despite Windows being primary. db.rs has no tests and Cargo.toml has no `[dev-dependencies]` block at all, so `tempfile`-style DB tests are genuinely un-enabled. schema_meta is created (db.rs:47) and referenced nowhere else — confirmed dead scaffolding. All six findings describe real, verifiable conditions; I confirmed five and adjusted one. The one material correction is in finding 5: version_gt does NOT parse '1.2.3-beta' as [1,2,3] and does NOT treat pre-release == release — non-numeric segments are silently DROPPED, so '1.2.3-beta' -> [1,2], and version_gt('1.2.3','1.2.3-beta') returns true (release ranks ABOVE its own pre-release). The conclusion (untested, real latent defect a test would catch, decide pre-release semantics) stands, but the stated mechanism was wrong, so I adjusted it rather than confirming as-written. I also note two small additions the recommendations should fold in: resample panics on EMPTY input (samples.len()-1 underflows) not just len-1, and the CSV finding's 'timestamp not escaped' sub-claim is technically true but harmless (it's truncated to a 19-char ISO prefix, not user input) — the real and valid risk in that finding is formula/CSV injection on the text field. Severities and efforts are well-calibrated; I left them intact except where noted.

verified_findings.title: No CI gate runs cargo test / clippy / eslint — the 19 passing tests never block a merge or release
verified_findings.detail: Verified against the live file. The sole workflow triggers on `push: tags: v*` and `workflow_dispatch`, runs on `macos-14`, and its steps are checkout -> setup-node -> setup-rust -> caches -> `npm ci` -> prepare-resources-macos.sh -> `npx tauri build --target aarch64-apple-darwin` -> upload artifacts -> draft release. There is no `cargo test`, no `cargo clippy`, no `cargo fmt --check`, and no `npm run lint`/`npm run build` step, and no `push`/`pull_request` branch trigger. I confirmed the 19 Rust tests pass (`cargo test` -> `test result: ok. 19 passed`), so they are advisory only — a regression in version_gt, trial cap, verify_token, or fingerprint_from would sail to a tag build with nothing red. I also confirmed `grep -rn runs-on .github/` returns ONLY `macos-14`: there is no Windows build job at all, so the primary platform's binary is never built or tested by automation. A `lint` script exists in package.json (eslint .) but nothing runs it.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add a `ci.yml` triggered on `push` and `pull_request` with: (1) a matrix job on windows-latest + ubuntu-latest (or macos-14) running `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`; (2) a node job running `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run build`. The tested modules are pure (no whisper model/GPU needed) so these run in a few minutes. Add a windows-latest build job mirroring the macOS one. Optionally make the tag-build depend on the test job. Caveat: a full `cargo test` will compile the tauri/cpal/windows crates on the matrix; if that is slow, scope the gate to `cargo test` (the 4 pure modules) plus `cargo build` rather than a full build on every push.
verified_findings.impact: Converts the existing 19 tests from decoration into an actual merge/release gate and is the only mechanism by which a `cfg(target_os)` Windows compile break is caught at PR time instead of at tag-build. Highest-leverage single change for audit safety.
verified_findings.risk: Low. Purely additive workflow file; worst case a flaky job, mark non-required initially.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Directly serves the dual-platform mandate: today ONLY macOS compiles in CI (confirmed). A windows-latest + ubuntu/macos matrix is the only automated way the team learns a platform-specific branch failed to compile. The pure tested modules are platform-agnostic so the test job is identical across OSes; the value of the matrix is the per-OS BUILD/clippy, which must include windows-latest to cover the WMI/SendInput/cfg(windows) code.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified the workflow file verbatim, confirmed no other workflow exists, confirmed 19 tests pass, and confirmed `runs-on` is macos-14 only (no Windows job). Only feasibility nuance I add: a FULL cargo test/clippy on the matrix compiles tauri+cpal+windows crates which is heavier than the finding's '<3 min' estimate for the build legs — but the cheap win (test the 4 pure modules) is real and fast. Recommendation lightly expanded; severity high is correct.

verified_findings.title: Ed25519 activation token verification (verify_token) has zero tests despite being security-critical and full of branch logic
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/activation.rs:33 verify_token (and is_activated:20); test module at :240 only covers memoization timing + the SHA pin
verified_findings.detail: Verified line by line. verify_token (activation.rs:33) is the licensing gate and has the branches the finding lists: parts.len() != 3 -> 'Malformed token' (:35); sig_bytes.len() != 64 -> 'Invalid signature length' (:40); Ed25519 `verifying_key.verify` failure -> 'Signature verification failed' (:48); mfp compared via `eq_ignore_ascii_case` (:55) -> 'Machine fingerprint mismatch'; `exp` present and `now > exp + 7*86_400` -> 'Activation token expired' (:63-68); and the legacy no-exp path that stays valid forever (:59-62 comment + the `if let Some(exp)` only running when exp exists). The only two tests in the file (:248, :264) cover memoization timing and the SHA-256 pipe-join vector — none exercise verify_token. Confirmed this is the single most consequential untested unit. The finding is right that all NON-happy branches are testable offline with the embedded PUB_KEY and hand-crafted token strings (no signing key needed); the happy path needs one offline-generated valid vector. is_activated (:20) reads the token file and delegates to verify_token, so a verify_token regression directly flips licensed-state.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add unit tests in activation.rs: malformed token (2 parts) -> Err; non-base64url part[2] -> Err; sig length != 64 -> Err; tampered signature -> Err; mfp mismatch -> Err (and confirm eq_ignore_ascii_case so case-different mfp still matches); exp boundary — token with exp = now-1 still valid (within grace), exp = now - 7*86400 - 10 -> expired; legacy token with NO exp -> Ok. Pin one offline-signed happy-path vector (mirrors the existing SHA vector pattern). For the exp-boundary tests, prefer crafting a token whose exp is computed relative to chrono::Utc::now() at test time over injecting a `now` param, to avoid touching the production signature.
verified_findings.impact: Protects revenue-gating logic and the explicit 'never brick existing customers' invariant (the no-exp legacy path). Catches an expiry/grace flip or an mfp-comparison regression before release.
verified_findings.risk: Low — pure-function tests, no side effects. Only effort is generating one valid happy-path vector.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: verify_token is platform-agnostic (confirmed: no cfg in the function), so one suite covers Windows and macOS. The mfp it compares differs per platform but the comparison logic under test does not — this is the safest high-value coverage to add for both targets at once. No macOS/Windows divergence risk in the test or fix.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Read all six branches at the cited lines; counts and line numbers match. One subtlety worth flagging for whoever writes the tests: a token with `exp` present but non-integer (as_i64 returns None) silently SKIPS the expiry check and is treated as never-expiring — that's an additional untested edge the suite should pin. Severity high and effort small are correct.

verified_findings.title: Fingerprint silently collapses to a shared constant when all hardware probes fail — no test, no guard
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/activation.rs:132-153 raw_fingerprint_components + wmi_value:156 / mac_ioreg_serial:186, mac_hw_model:206, mac_disk_serial:219 (each returns "UNKNOWN" on any failure); fingerprint_from:126
verified_findings.detail: Verified. Each Windows probe (wmi_value:156, plus the OEM-placeholder filter at :169 that maps empty / 'To Be Filled By O.E.M.' / 'Default string' -> 'UNKNOWN') and each macOS probe (mac_ioreg_serial:199, mac_hw_model:212, mac_disk_serial:234) independently returns the literal 'UNKNOWN' on any failure. raw_fingerprint_components (:133/:142) collects exactly three of these, and fingerprint_from (:126) does SHA256(components.join('|')). So on a locked-down box where all three resolve to 'UNKNOWN', the fingerprint is SHA256('UNKNOWN|UNKNOWN|UNKNOWN') — identical across every such machine. Consequences are as stated: (a) a token bound to one all-UNKNOWN machine validates on any other all-UNKNOWN machine (binding defeated for that class), and (b) per-machine activation/trial accounting collides for whole classes of corporate/VM/sandboxed machines. There is no guard counting resolved components and no test asserting a degenerate set is detected. The non-windows/non-macos stub (:151) ALSO returns all-UNKNOWN by design, reinforcing the path exists.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add a `component_quality()` helper (count of non-'UNKNOWN' components) and a guard in machine_fingerprint: if < 2 of 3 resolve, fall back to a persisted random UUID stored in the data dir (uuid v4 is ALREADY a dependency — Cargo.toml:23 has uuid features=['v4'], and dirs is present for the data dir) so the install is still stable but unique, and/or surface an activation error. CRITICAL constraint: this must be ADDITIVE — only change behavior for the all/mostly-UNKNOWN case — because any machine whose CURRENT fingerprint legitimately contains one 'UNKNOWN' component already has a token bound to that hash; re-deriving it would brick that token (the same 'never brick existing customers' invariant the file comments protect). Add tests on fingerprint_from / component_quality proving all-UNKNOWN is flagged and that two machines sharing one component still differ. Coordinate with the activation server to reject an all-UNKNOWN machineHash.
verified_findings.impact: Closes a licensing-bypass vector AND a support-load failure mode (machine-class collisions). Turns a latent multi-machine correctness bug into a tested, guarded path.
verified_findings.risk: Medium — must be additive (only the all/mostly-UNKNOWN case) to avoid re-binding existing tokens whose hash already contains one UNKNOWN component. The persisted-UUID fallback adds a new on-disk file in the shared data dir, which the resident app also reads — choose a filename that won't collide.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Symmetric failure across platforms (Windows WMI restriction vs macOS ioreg/diskutil sandboxing both yield 'UNKNOWN' — confirmed both impls do this), so the guard and tests must cover both raw_fingerprint_components impls. The UUID fallback is platform-neutral (uuid+dirs already cross-platform deps), making it the cleanest dual-platform fix. Do NOT make the fallback platform-specific.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified all three Windows and three macOS probes default to 'UNKNOWN', and that fingerprint_from is a plain SHA256 of the pipe-join with no quality check. The bypass severity is real but bounded: the attacker must ALSO be on an all-UNKNOWN machine (you can't forge a victim's real hardware hash this way), so the dominant practical harm is the collision/accounting failure, not arbitrary license theft — the finding already frames (b) as 'more likely in practice', which is accurate. I confirmed uuid v4 + dirs are already deps, so the recommended fallback needs no new crate. Severity high and effort medium are right; left intact.

verified_findings.title: Frontend has no test runner and zero tests — ~3700 LOC including the Dashboard state machine is fully unverified
verified_findings.location: src/ (18 files; Dashboard.jsx 488, SettingsPanel.jsx 960, Onboarding.jsx 321, LicenseGate.jsx 241); package.json has no vitest/jest/@testing-library; SettingsPanel.jsx:655 eslint-disable react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
verified_findings.detail: Verified. No `.test.*`/`.spec.*` files exist under src/ (the grep hits for 'it('/'test' are JSX prose, not tests). package.json devDependencies (read directly) contain eslint + vite + @vitejs/plugin-react but NO vitest/jest/@testing-library/jsdom — there is literally no way to run a frontend test today. The eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps at SettingsPanel.jsx:655 is confirmed present (a classic stale-closure hazard a test would pin). The constraint the finding leans on is real and in memory: the resident tray app must not be GUI-tested via `tauri dev`, so the most regression-prone code (Dashboard state machine, beep/listener wiring) has BOTH no automated tests AND a constrained manual path.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add vitest + @testing-library/react + jsdom as devDependencies and a `test` script (vitest reuses vite.config — near zero-config with the existing @vitejs/plugin-react). Write a thin module mock for `@tauri-apps/api` invoke/listen, then cover the Dashboard state machine first: hotkey-toggle re-entrancy (rapid toggles must not start-then-immediately-stop), status transitions, and the inflight guard. This is the highest-value frontend coverage because the documented bugs cluster there. Bonus: a render assertion on platform-conditional copy guards against platform-string leakage.
verified_findings.impact: Creates the missing safety net for the most bug-prone area and lets the team verify Dashboard logic WITHOUT launching a GUI against the resident tray app (honoring the do-not-GUI-test constraint).
verified_findings.risk: Low — additive tooling; vitest reuses vite.config. Main one-time cost is the Tauri IPC mock.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Frontend tests run in jsdom on any OS, validating the shared UI for both Windows and macOS in one run. The mock approach is OS-neutral. Practical note: assertions on platform-conditional rendered copy (the 'AppData' vs macOS-path strings the journal mentions) are exactly what catches platform-string regressions that otherwise only surface on the other OS at runtime.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed no test framework in package.json (read it fully), no test files, and the SettingsPanel:655 eslint-disable line. Severity medium (not high) is the right call: this is a large, genuinely useful net but it is additive scaffolding, not a live defect — nothing is currently broken by its absence, unlike the untested verify_token where a silent regression has direct revenue/lockout impact. Left medium intact.

verified_findings.title: Pure hot-path and release-path functions are untested despite being trivially testable (resample, version_gt, model_name_from_file)
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/audio.rs:354 resample; src-tauri/src/updater.rs:162 version_gt; src-tauri/src/whisper.rs:647 model_name_from_file & :629 model_label
verified_findings.detail: All three functions verified pure and untested. CORRECTION to the version_gt claim: the finding states '1.2.3-beta parses as [1,2,3]' and 'a pre-release would be treated equal to the release' — both are FALSE. I traced the actual code: parse() does `s.split('.').filter_map(|p| p.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())`, so the segment '3-beta' fails parse::<u32> and is DROPPED, giving '1.2.3-beta' -> [1,2] (NOT [1,2,3]). Consequently version_gt('1.2.3','1.2.3-beta') returns TRUE (the release outranks its own pre-release, since [1,2,3] > [1,2]), and version_gt('1.2.3-beta','1.2.3') returns FALSE. So a pre-release is treated as STRICTLY LOWER than the release, not equal. I confirmed the benign cases too: 1.2.10 > 1.2.9 = true, and 1.2 vs 1.2.0 are equal (both gt false). resample (audio.rs:354) is pure `&[f32],u32,u32 -> Vec<f32>` and does `samples[idx.min(samples.len()-1)]` — which PANICS on EMPTY input because samples.len()-1 underflows usize (the finding's 'no panic on len-1 input' misses the real edge: empty slice). model_name_from_file (whisper.rs:647) and model_label (:629) confirmed pure, with the -q5_0/-q5_1/-q8_0 + .en suffix stripping that's easy to get wrong and has no vector tests.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add #[cfg(test)] units. version_gt: pin 1.2.10 > 1.2.9, 1.2 == 1.2.0 (both gt false), equal returns false, AND explicitly test/DECIDE pre-release: assert the ACTUAL behavior (version_gt('1.2.3','1.2.3-beta')==true; version_gt('1.2.3-beta','1.2.3')==false) and decide whether a '-beta' suffix on the SERVER's latest version (which would make it look OLDER than a plain release and suppress a real update) is acceptable — if not, fix parse to not drop the numeric prefix of a mixed segment. resample: assert len ≈ s.len()*to/from, identity when from==to, monotonic interpolation between two known samples, AND a guard/test for EMPTY input (currently panics — either return empty early or it's an audio-corruption-adjacent crash). model_name_from_file: pin 'ggml-medium-q5_0.bin'->'medium', 'ggml-base.en.bin'->'base', unknown passthrough.
verified_findings.impact: Cheap, high-confidence coverage of an audio path that PANICS on empty input and an updater comparison sitting next to a tracked CRITICAL. version_gt does have a latent pre-release defect a test surfaces — just not the one originally described.
verified_findings.risk: None for adding tests — pure functions. The resample empty-input panic, if the team chooses to fix it, is a one-line early-return; verify no caller relies on the current panic (none should).
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: All three are platform-agnostic; one suite covers Windows and macOS. version_gt is especially worth pinning because the updater downloads platform-specific installers (.dmg vs .exe, updater.rs:63-67) gated on this same comparison — a comparison bug suppresses or forces updates identically on both platforms.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Adjusted because the finding's version_gt MECHANISM is factually wrong — I compiled and ran the exact parse/version_gt logic: '1.2.3-beta' -> [1,2] (segment dropped), NOT [1,2,3], and pre-release ranks BELOW (not equal to) the release. The audit's conclusion (untested, real latent defect, decide pre-release semantics) survives, so this stays a valid finding, but the detail and recommendation are corrected and I added the genuine resample EMPTY-input panic the original missed (its 'len-1' edge is fine; len==0 underflows). Severity medium / effort trivial unchanged.

verified_findings.title: db.rs migrations, FTS5 triggers, and CSV export are untested and have a latent CSV-injection/quoting gap
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/db.rs: open/migration:78-87, FTS5 triggers:62-71, export csv:227-239, prune_backups:268
verified_findings.detail: Verified. db.rs is 288 lines of stateful SQLite with zero tests, and I confirmed Cargo.toml has NO [dev-dependencies] block at all, so tempfile/DB tests are un-enabled. (1) schema_meta is CREATEd at :47 and `grep -rn schema_meta src-tauri` returns ONLY that line — confirmed dead scaffolding, never written or read, while the actual migration (:84) is column-presence-based with no version tracking. (2) FTS5 triggers (:62-71) must stay in sync with the table; a schema change forgetting one silently desyncs search, untested. (3) CSV export (:228-238): the text field IS quote-escaped (`replace('"','""')`, :233) but there is NO formula-injection guard — a transcript beginning with '=', '+', '-', or '@' becomes a live formula when the CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets (the quoted-cell wrapper does not prevent Excel formula evaluation). The finding's secondary claim that the TIMESTAMP field is unescaped is technically true but practically harmless: line :232 truncates it to `.get(..19)` (a 19-char ISO prefix YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) which cannot contain a quote and is not user-controlled — so drop that sub-claim; the formula-injection on `text` is the real, valid risk. (4) prune_backups (:268-288) relies on lexicographic filename sort == chronological (filenames are transcripts_%Y%m%d_%H%M%S.db, so this holds for same-century timestamps) — untested but correct as written.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add `tempfile` (or in-memory `Connection::open_in_memory`) as a dev-dependency and write DB tests against a THROWAWAY DB (never the real data dir — the resident app shares com.alan.echo): insert rows, assert FTS search finds them and survives update/delete (trigger correctness); open a legacy DB missing raw_text and assert the migration backfills (:84-86); assert CSV export round-trips text with quotes/commas/newlines. FIX the formula injection: prefix any text cell beginning with =,+,-,@ with a leading apostrophe or space inside the quotes. Decide schema_meta: either wire it into a real versioned migration runner or delete the dead table.
verified_findings.impact: Protects transcript-data integrity and search, removes a real (low-severity) formula-injection vector, and resolves dead migration scaffolding so the next schema change has a tested path.
verified_findings.risk: Low — tests use throwaway/in-memory DBs. The CSV fix is a one-line prefix guard; the schema_meta decision is a small refactor.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: rusqlite 'bundled' is identical on both platforms (Cargo.toml:18), so DB tests validate both at once. Mandatory caveat the finding correctly raises: tests MUST use a temp dir / in-memory DB, never the real data dir, or `cargo test` would clobber the user's live transcript DB that the resident tray app holds open (and WAL-mode concurrent access from a test could even corrupt it).
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Adjusted to correct one sub-claim: the 'timestamp field not escaped' point is true-but-harmless (it's a 19-char ISO prefix via .get(..19), not user input — can't contain a quote), so I demoted it and centered the finding on the genuinely valid formula-injection on the text field, which I confirmed has no =/+/-/@ guard. Everything else verified exactly: zero db tests, no [dev-dependencies] block, schema_meta dead (single grep hit), column-based migration, in-place FTS triggers. Severity medium / effort medium unchanged; the core finding is real and the temp-dir caveat is critical given the resident app.

verified_findings.title: Audio recorder, whisper lifecycle, and paste are integration-only and effectively untestable as written — no seam for testing
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/audio.rs:130 recorder_thread (channel state machine); src-tauri/src/whisper.rs (Inner/Status state machine, free_port:552); src-tauri/src/paste.rs
verified_findings.detail: Verified. recorder_thread (audio.rs:130) is a channel-driven state machine holding `recording: bool` plus samples/has_speech/rms_level mutexes, welded to cpal device enumeration and build_input_stream callbacks — no test seam. The mono-downmix + RMS + max_samples-cap logic is genuinely duplicated across THREE format branches: F32 (:187), I16 (:212), and U16 (confirmed present at :233) — a DRY hazard, since a fix to one must be hand-mirrored to the other two. free_port (whisper.rs:552) binds real TcpListeners across BASE_PORT..+20, so it's the one near-pure bit but still touches sockets. The whisper Inner/Status transitions and generation-supersession, and paste.rs's foreground-window capture + SendInput, are OS-bound. The journal-documented gnarly bugs (orphaned servers, paste into wrong window, abandoned recordings) live here. The finding's framing (structural debt; extract pure helpers rather than chase unit tests first) is sound.
verified_findings.recommendation: Don't chase unit tests on the I/O first. Extract the decision logic so it becomes testable: (a) pull the downmix + RMS + cap math out of the three audio callbacks into pure helpers (downmix_to_mono(data,channels), rms(&[f32]), cap_extend(buf,mono,max)) and unit-test those — this ALSO de-duplicates the 3x copy; (b) model the whisper Status transition table + generation-supersession rule as a pure function and test it; (c) for genuinely OS-bound paste/device code, add #[ignore]-by-default integration tests runnable on a dev box; track the rest as known integration-test debt with the journal's regression checklist as the manual smoke list.
verified_findings.impact: Makes the highest-bug-density code progressively testable without a risky rewrite, and removes the 3x-copied audio-callback maintenance hazard.
verified_findings.risk: Medium — extracting helpers from the live audio callbacks touches the hot path; must preserve EXACT arithmetic (the i16/u16 normalization /32768.0 and the WAV-write clamp) so output bytes don't change. Do under TDD with golden-sample assertions; verify the resident app still records correctly after the refactor (but NOT via tauri dev — use the installed build or a separate data dir).
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: paste.rs (Windows SendInput/UIPI vs macOS paste) and device enumeration are the most platform-divergent code in the repo; the extractable helpers (downmix/rms/cap, status transitions) are platform-neutral and testable once on either OS, while the thin OS shims stay integration-only per platform. Prioritize the neutral extraction so both platforms benefit from one suite — and ensure the refactor compiles on BOTH (this is exactly the class of dual-platform break the missing CI would catch).
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified recorder_thread structure, free_port binding real sockets, and the THREE-way duplication (F32:187 / I16:212 / U16:233) the DRY claim rests on. Severity low is right (this is forward-looking structural debt, not a live defect) and effort large is honest — the extraction touches the audio hot path and must be byte-exact. No correction needed; the recommendation to extract-then-test rather than mock the hardware is the correct sequencing.

summary: Verified all 10 findings against the source. The summary's factual spine is accurate: spawn_server passes only -m/--host/--port/-l/-t/-sns with no prompt/VAD/streaming (whisper.rs:497-504); hotkeys are hardcoded literals with no set_hotkey in the invoke_handler (main.rs:1053-1065, 1100-1140); register_emit_hotkey ignores key-up (main.rs:720); macOS detect_nvidia_gpu always returns None and find_server_binary/resolve_model can only ever reach a CPU build on Mac (whisper.rs:601-604, 383-395); text_cleanup strips newlines in normalize_whitespace (text_cleanup.rs:103) so no spoken formatting exists; transcripts are one flat FTS-backed table with no tag/folder column (db.rs:37-45) rendered as one Load-more list (Dashboard.jsx:374-390); StatusPanel shows a fixed 30%-width indeterminate bar (StatusPanel.jsx:60-64); deliver_text take()s the paste target and auto_paste is a single global bool (main.rs:451-452); has_speech is a boolean RMS flag with no trimming and the full resampled buffer is written to WAV (audio.rs:195, 288-321). Eight findings are CONFIRMED. Two are ADJUSTED: finding 1 (custom vocabulary) — the highest-ROI claim holds, but its preferred per-request `prompt` HTTP-form path is NOT proven against the bundled whisper-server in this repo (the code only ever POSTs file+response_format); I down-rank that to a secondary option behind the certain --prompt engine-flag path and keep severity high. Finding 9 (per-app paste) — real and feasible, but its dual-platform note understates that resolving the macOS app NAME needs an extra osascript process spawn, the exact class of cost the fingerprint fix removed; severity stays low and I tighten the recommendation to cache/derive identity without a per-record spawn. No finding is rejected — none is already-handled or infeasible. The biggest genuine dual-platform liability (no Metal on Mac, finding 2) is correctly identified and correctly scoped as additive/macOS-gated.

verified_findings.title: Custom vocabulary / dictionary via whisper-server initial_prompt — highest-ROI accuracy feature
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: spawn_server (whisper.rs:497-504) passes only -m/--host/--port/-l/-t/-sns; no initial_prompt anywhere. post_inference (whisper.rs:515-549) builds the multipart body with exactly two fields — `file` and `response_format=json` — and NOTHING else. ALWAYS_UPPERCASE/ALWAYS_CAPITALIZE (text_cleanup.rs:24-38) are hardcoded developer lists that only fix casing of already-correct words; nyse/nasdaq/etf/ipo are indeed pre-seeded (line 29), confirming the finance-audience point. There is no user-editable vocabulary path. The accuracy gap is real and this is the cheapest lever.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add a `custom_vocabulary` setting (newline/comma separated). PRIMARY (certain) path: build an initial_prompt string and pass whisper-server the `--prompt`/`-p` CLI flag in spawn_server on engine start; vocabulary edits then take effect on the existing reload() machinery (main.rs:116-123, which already restarts the engine for whisper_model/language). SECONDARY (only if validated against the bundled server build): add a `prompt` form field to post_inference's multipart body for per-request, restart-free injection — but DO NOT assume this works; the current server is only ever sent file+response_format, and whether this whisper-server accepts a `prompt` form field must be confirmed first. Also feed the same terms into text_cleanup's capitalization pass. Add a Settings 'Vocabulary' textarea near Text cleanup (SettingsPanel.jsx ~327). Cap ~200 tokens to protect latency.
verified_findings.impact: Directly raises perceived accuracy on the exact words users care about; strongest single differentiator vs CPU whisper.cpp wrappers and the clearest paid-tier story.
verified_findings.risk: Over-long prompts add latency and can bias output (cap tokens). The cited per-request prompt-field route is unverified against the shipped server — leading with it risks shipping a no-op; the --prompt engine-flag route is the safe default. Reload-on-edit reuses the proven model/language restart path, so latency of a restart (already accepted elsewhere) is the only cost.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Pure whisper-server flag/form-field plus a settings string — identical on Windows and macOS, no cfg(target_os). Fully dual-platform. (Note: takes effect via the same reload() used for model/language, which is already cross-platform.)
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Kept as high/small — claim is correct and verified at the cited lines. ADJUSTED the recommendation: the finding's PREFERRED mechanism (per-request `prompt` field on /inference, called 'preferable') is not substantiated by this repo — post_inference (whisper.rs:518-525) hand-builds the multipart body with only file+response_format, and nothing tells me the bundled whisper-server accepts a `prompt` form field. I reordered to make the --prompt CLI flag (which whisper.cpp's server reliably supports) the primary path and demoted the form-field path to 'validate first.' Severity unchanged because either path delivers the feature cheaply.

verified_findings.title: macOS has zero GPU acceleration — every Mac runs CPU-only while competitors ship Metal
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/whisper.rs:600-605 (detect_nvidia_gpu macOS stub returns None); src-tauri/src/packs.rs:36-93 (only Cuda/Vulkan pack kinds)
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: on non-Windows, detect_nvidia_gpu() unconditionally returns (None,None) with the comment 'Metal/CoreML acceleration is a v2 item' (whisper.rs:600-605). Because hw.gpu_name is therefore always None on macOS, both resolve_model (whisper.rs:442 takes the CPU-core branches) and find_server_binary (whisper.rs:388-395 takes the non-GPU candidate list, and the only macOS-reachable binary is the plain `whisper-server`) can NEVER select a GPU build on Mac. packs.rs PackKind has exactly Cuda+Vulkan (packs.rs:37-40), both Windows-hosted URLs (packs.rs:80-81); no Apple offer exists. gpuVerdictText returns 'No dedicated GPU found' (SettingsPanel.jsx:553) which is actively wrong on Apple Silicon. The dual-platform parity gap is real and is the Mac build's weakest surface.
verified_findings.recommendation: Ship a Metal whisper-server as a third PackKind::Metal (or bundle directly on macOS — it has no cuBLAS-style external runtime). Add Apple-Silicon detection in detect_hardware (sysctl hw.optional.arm64 / machdep.cpu.brand_string) feeding a non-NVIDIA gpu signal, and have resolve_model/find_server_binary prefer the Metal binary on macOS. Fix gpuVerdictText (SettingsPanel.jsx:532-553) to name Apple Silicon instead of 'No dedicated GPU found.' Reuse the existing pack confirm/disable/rollback machinery as the model.
verified_findings.impact: Removes Echo's single largest macOS performance/perception deficit; turns the Mac build from 'works' to 'fast,' matching Superwhisper/MacWhisper.
verified_findings.risk: Requires producing/signing/notarizing a Metal whisper-server and validating across macOS versions. binary_kind() (whisper.rs:557-566) only recognizes cuda_release/vulkan_release/cpu, so a 'metal' kind must be threaded through it AND through the engine_kind reporting the UI keys off — otherwise GPU verdict/streaming-estimate text stays wrong on Mac even after the binary lands. find_server_binary's macOS branch (whisper.rs:388-395) must gain the Metal candidate or detection alone changes nothing.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: This finding IS the dual-platform gap: Windows has CUDA+Vulkan, macOS has nothing. All new code is macOS-gated and additive; the Windows path is untouched. Caveat: binary_kind() and engine_kind plumbing are shared and must learn 'metal' or the cross-platform UI/estimate code stays Mac-blind.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed at every cited line. Severity high and effort medium are right — the binary/notarization work is the real cost, code wiring is modest. I add the binary_kind()/engine_kind plumbing caveat (whisper.rs:557-566) the finding omitted, since detection-without-wiring is a common half-fix; this strengthens rather than weakens the finding. No platform regression risk to Windows.

verified_findings.title: No selectable / rebindable hotkeys — accelerators are fully hardcoded
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/main.rs:1053-1075 (literal 'CmdOrCtrl+Shift+Space' etc.); SettingsPanel.jsx:364-382 (Hotkeys section is read-only display)
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: toggle/cancel/show accelerators are string literals registered once in setup() (main.rs:1053-1065). The invoke_handler list (main.rs:1100-1140) contains get_hotkey_info but NO set_hotkey command. SettingsPanel HotkeyRow (SettingsPanel.jsx:810-820) renders label+keys spans only — no edit affordance, no onClick, no capture input. On registration failure the UI's only advice is 'Use the tray menu's Start Dictation' (SettingsPanel.jsx:375) / 'use the tray menu' (Onboarding/Dashboard). Users cannot pick a working key. This is table-stakes for a global-hotkey product and is the direct fix for the 'Unavailable' dead-end the app surfaces in three places.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add a set_hotkey(action, accelerator) command that unregisters the old accel, registers the new via register_emit_hotkey (main.rs:716), persists to settings, and updates state.hotkeys (main.rs:1070). Read toggle/show accels from settings at startup with the current literals as defaults. In SettingsPanel turn HotkeyRow into a key-capture control validated by a dry register/unregister exactly like the cancel-accel probe (main.rs:1054-1064).
verified_findings.impact: Eliminates the most common 'hotkey doesn't work' support case and matches a baseline competitor capability; unblocks users whose combo is taken (incl. the IME collision on Ctrl+Shift+Space).
verified_findings.risk: Must validate the chord registers before committing (the cancel probe at main.rs:1056-1063 is the exact safe pattern). Persist the raw 'CmdOrCtrl+...' form, not the display string, or display_accel (main.rs:736) double-maps. The cancel hotkey is special — it is intentionally registered only per-recording (main.rs:1050-1051, 300-302), so a rebind UI for cancel must persist the accel but keep the register/unregister-around-recording lifecycle, not register it system-wide.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: register_emit_hotkey and tauri-plugin-global-shortcut are cross-platform; display_accel already maps CmdOrCtrl per-OS (main.rs:737). A rebind UI works identically on both as long as the raw 'CmdOrCtrl+...' form is persisted so per-OS display keeps working.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed: no set_hotkey exists in the handler, HotkeyRow is display-only. Severity high / effort small are justified — the safe-probe and state.hotkeys plumbing already exist. I add one correctness guardrail the finding glossed: cancel is deliberately a per-recording registration, so a naive rebind that registers it system-wide would change behavior; persist-but-preserve-lifecycle. Doesn't change the verdict.

verified_findings.title: No push-to-talk (hold-to-talk) mode — only press-toggle
verified_findings.location: src/components/Dashboard.jsx:175-234 (handleToggle state machine); src-tauri/src/main.rs:716-733 (register_emit_hotkey only acts on ShortcutState::Pressed)
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: register_emit_hotkey reacts only to ev.state==ShortcutState::Pressed (main.rs:720) and discards Released. handleToggle is a strict toggle keyed off statusRef (Dashboard.jsx:175-234), serialized by inflightRef (Dashboard.jsx:165-177). ShortcutState carries Pressed/Released, so the plumbing for a hold variant exists. Competitors offer hold-to-talk, often as default. Real gap, medium severity.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add a 'Hotkey behavior: Toggle | Hold to talk' setting. In register_emit_hotkey, when hold mode is on for the toggle accel, emit 'dictate-start' on Pressed and 'dictate-stop' on Released; map those to the start/stop branches of the existing state machine (it already serializes via inflightRef). Reuse the held-Shift mitigation already in paste.rs:115-124. Keep Toggle the default.
verified_findings.impact: Faster flow for short dictations and a familiar mode for competitor switchers; low friction because it reuses the recorder and state machine.
verified_findings.risk: Global-shortcut key-up can be dropped on focus change; add a max-duration backstop — VERIFIED to already exist (MAX_RECORDING_SECONDS=300 Dashboard.jsx:16,156; MAX_RECORD_SECONDS=310 audio.rs:15,174). register_emit_hotkey currently closes over a `&'static str event`; a hold variant emitting two different events (start/stop) needs the closure reworked to branch on state, a small but non-trivial signature change. The inflightRef guard (Dashboard.jsx:176) returns early on re-entrancy — a fast press/release could land start and stop close enough that the stop is dropped; the hold mapping must not rely on the same early-return semantics as toggle.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: tauri-plugin-global-shortcut delivers Pressed/Released on both OSes; no platform-specific code. Verify macOS release-event reliability where modifier-only releases can be lossy — the backstop covers the lost-release case on both platforms.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed at the cited lines incl. the Pressed-only filter and the existing backstops. Kept medium/small. I flag two real implementation snags the finding underplays: register_emit_hotkey's &'static str event closure must be reworked to emit two events, and the inflightRef early-return could swallow a fast hold-release stop. Neither is a blocker; verdict stands.

verified_findings.title: No spoken formatting/punctuation commands ('new line', 'comma', 'new paragraph')
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: clean() (text_cleanup.rs:70-100) handles fillers/repetitions/capitalization/acronyms but has no spoken-command pass. Worse for the feature: normalize_whitespace (text_cleanup.rs:102-104) actively REPLACES \n and \r with spaces and collapses runs, so even if a newline were introduced upstream it would be flattened — any 'new line' support must insert breaks AFTER normalize_whitespace or be exempted from it. Echo pastes a single block, so no line breaks are possible today. Real gap for lists/code-comments/chat — the developer use case.
verified_findings.recommendation:
Add an opt-in command pass at the END of clean() (after normalize_whitespace and after the final fix_capitalization at text_cleanup.rs:97, so inserted breaks survive): 'new line'->
, 'new paragraph'->

, 'comma'->',', 'period'/'full stop'->'.', 'open/close quote', 'bullet'->'- '. Off by default (users dictate the literal words), English-gated (gate on language=='en'). Add a test mirroring levels_visibly_differ_on_settings_sample (text_cleanup.rs:356). Verify the auto-paste path and SQLite store preserve embedded newlines.
verified_findings.impact: Unlocks lists, multi-line messages, code-comment dictation; meaningfully closes the gap to Dragon/Wispr for structured text.
verified_findings.risk: Ambiguity ('I paused for a comma'); must be opt-in and English-gated, with ordering rules vs custom vocabulary. CRITICAL correctness catch the finding missed: normalize_whitespace (text_cleanup.rs:103) strips \n, and the final_cleanup/normalize ordering means a command pass placed too early gets erased — it must run last and the WAV->paste pipeline (SendInput sends a clipboard paste, so embedded \n survive; verify osascript keystroke path on mac preserves them) must carry the newline through.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Pure Rust string processing in text_cleanup.rs — platform-agnostic. One cross-platform caveat: confirm embedded newlines survive both paste backends (Windows clipboard Ctrl+V preserves them; macOS osascript 'keystroke v using command down' pastes the clipboard so it also preserves them — but worth a spot-check, since the mac path is osascript not SendInput).
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed and strengthened. The finding's core is right; I add the load-bearing detail it omitted: normalize_whitespace (line 103) deletes newlines, so a command pass MUST run last or it is a no-op — this is the kind of ordering bug that ships broken. Kept medium/medium. Also flagged the newline-survives-paste verification on both backends as a dual-platform check.

verified_findings.title: No transcript folders / tags despite a flat, paginating single list
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/db.rs:37-51 (transcripts schema has no tag/folder column); src/components/Dashboard.jsx:373-391 (one flat list); src-tauri/src/db.rs:127-164 (search)
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: the transcripts table (db.rs:37-45) has id/timestamp/text/raw_text/duration/char/word columns only — no tag/folder/pin/favorite. The list renders one chronological displayList with 'Load more' pagination (Dashboard.jsx:374-390) and the only retrieval is FTS5 search. An additive ALTER migration template exists (db.rs:84-87 for raw_text). Real organization gap; retention/'serious tool' feature, not a recording feature.
verified_findings.recommendation: Start minimal: a `pinned` (or `favorite`) boolean is a one-column additive ALTER following the db.rs:84-87 template, plus a get_transcripts filter and a star toggle on TranscriptCard — 80% of value for a fraction of effort. Tags/folders (a tags table + junction, a get_transcripts tag filter, chip UI near SearchBar) can follow. Ensure export (db.rs export path) includes the new field.
verified_findings.impact: Turns a growing history from a liability into an asset; supports power users keeping snippets/templates. Fits ALAN's workspace positioning.
verified_findings.risk: Schema migration + filter interaction with FTS5 (the FTS triggers at db.rs:62-71 mirror only `text`; a tag column doesn't touch FTS, so a tag FILTER must be applied as a normal WHERE on the base table joined to FTS results, not added to the FTS index). Keep migrations additive. The 'pin boolean first' staging keeps risk low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: SQLite + React only — no platform-specific code. Identical on Windows and macOS.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed: schema and flat list match the claims. Kept medium/medium. I sharpen the FTS interaction note (the existing triggers index only `text`, so tags live outside FTS and must be a WHERE join) and endorse the finding's own 'pin boolean first' as the right risk-reducing path. No change to verdict; the finding already proposes the cheap staging.

verified_findings.title: No streaming / partial transcription — user stares at a blank 'Transcribing...' bar
verified_findings.location: src/components/StatusPanel.jsx:47-68 (indeterminate processing bar); src-tauri/src/whisper.rs:302-343 (single blocking POST); src-tauri/src/main.rs:409-444 (transcribe awaits whole result)
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: transcribe (main.rs:409-444) awaits one spawn_blocking that does state.whisper.transcribe -> post_inference, a single blocking multipart POST of the whole WAV (whisper.rs:515-549) returning only on completion. StatusPanel processing state (StatusPanel.jsx:47-66) renders a fixed width:'30%' bar with a looping echo-bar animation — genuinely indeterminate, no text until done. For long CPU dictations this is seconds of dead air. Phase-1 (determinate estimate) is cheap; true streaming is large.
verified_findings.recommendation: Phase 1 (small): replace the fixed-30%-width indeterminate bar (StatusPanel.jsx:61-64) with a duration-based estimate using known clip length (recording.duration_seconds is already returned, Dashboard.jsx:195) and a realtime factor keyed off engine_kind/cpu_cores so the bar actually advances. Phase 2 (large): for clips over N seconds, segment the WAV and POST sequentially, emitting partial text via a Tauri event the Dashboard appends. Reserve live partial-decode for later.
verified_findings.impact: Removes perceived latency on long dictations; phase 1 is nearly free and improves the most-watched moment.
verified_findings.risk: Chunking splits words mid-utterance and hurts boundary accuracy (needs overlap/stitching). Phase-1 estimate is low-risk but must key the realtime factor off the ACTUAL compute path (engine_kind) — and per finding 2, macOS has no GPU path, so a naive estimate would over-promise on Mac; the estimate is only honest once engine_kind is correct on each OS. Effort 'large' is right for the finding as a whole; the valuable Phase-1 slice is actually 'small' and should be split out.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Engine/event plumbing identical on both OSes. The realtime-factor estimate MUST key off engine_kind (cpu/cuda/vulkan/future-metal) so the bar is honest on each OS's real compute path — and today every Mac is the cpu factor (finding 2), so the Mac estimate will read slow until Metal lands.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed the indeterminate bar and single-blocking-POST. I keep effort 'large' for the streaming whole, but the finding buries that its Phase-1 (honest progress bar) is independently shippable and SMALL/high-value — I call that out so it isn't lost behind the large label. Coupled the realtime-factor honesty to finding 2 (no Mac GPU). Adjusted to surface the cheap slice; the streaming claim itself is accurate, not rejected.

verified_findings.title: No undo-paste / clipboard-restore-on-demand after a bad auto-paste
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: deliver_text (main.rs:448-513) injects Ctrl+V via paste::paste_into into the captured target, and the toast says 'Pasted into your app' (Dashboard.jsx:221). The prior clipboard IS preserved for 1500ms on a detached thread (main.rs:493-503), so building blocks exist. But the paste target is consumed via .take() at main.rs:452, so any undo would need a retained copy. The transcript is saved (text not lost) but the destination now holds unwanted text with no one-click remedy. Real but low-severity polish.
verified_findings.recommendation: Prefer the SAFE variant the finding itself notes: a 'Re-dictate' / 'Copy correct text again' toast action that re-arms recording for the same target — avoids the Ctrl+Z-undoes-too-much hazard entirely. If pursuing true undo, retain (don't .take()) the paste target through a short undo window and send Ctrl+Z/Cmd+Z via the existing paste.rs per-OS path. Keep it low priority.
verified_findings.impact: Reduces misrecognition cost from 'manually fix in the other app' to one click; improves auto-paste trust.
verified_findings.risk: Ctrl+Z behavior varies per target app and can undo more than the paste — the re-dictate/re-copy variant sidesteps this and is the recommended path. Retaining the paste target past .take() (main.rs:452) needs care so it can't go stale and paste-undo into the wrong window after a focus change.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Undo keystroke differs per OS (Ctrl+Z vs Cmd+Z) and must reuse paste.rs's per-platform SendInput (win) / osascript (mac) paths, both of which exist. Symmetric work. The macOS osascript path spawns a process per keystroke-send (paste.rs:176) — fine here since it's a user-initiated, off-hotpath action.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed: deliver_text injects Ctrl+V, toast claims paste, target is .take()n, prior clip held 1.5s. Kept low/medium. The finding already prefers the safe re-dictate variant over raw Ctrl+Z; I endorse that ordering since Ctrl+Z undo-scope is genuinely unsafe across apps. No change.

verified_findings.title: No per-app paste profiles (auto-paste is one global toggle)
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/main.rs:451 (auto_paste read as single global bool); src-tauri/src/paste.rs:28-30 / 142-157 (foreground_window already captures the target app)
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: auto_paste is a single global bool (main.rs:451; SettingsPanel.jsx:313). start_recording captures the foreground target (main.rs:272 -> paste::foreground_window). PARTIAL CORRECTION to the finding: on Windows, foreground_window() returns only the HWND (paste.rs:28-30) — the PID is fetched internally for integrity checks but NOT persisted, so 'app identity' is not currently captured on Windows, only the window handle. On macOS, foreground_window() does return the PID (paste.rs:142-157). Either way the identity is consumed/discarded (main.rs:452 take()). The per-app-profile gap is real; the finding slightly overstates how much identity is captured on Windows today.
verified_findings.recommendation: Resolve the target's app identity at DELIVER time (not start time): Windows GetWindowThreadProcessId->QueryFullProcessImageNameW (a cheap Win32 call, NOT WMI/PowerShell) on the retained HWND; macOS — derive the app name from the already-captured PID. Store an app->{auto_paste} override map in settings and consult it in deliver_text before the global default. Start with the auto-paste override only.
verified_findings.impact: Fixes 'auto-paste fights my terminal/editor' without a global off switch; foundation for per-context behavior.
verified_findings.risk: App-identity resolution adds a syscall on the deliver path — keep it OFF the beep-blocking start path. The macOS app-NAME resolution is the real hazard: deriving a name from the PID requires ANOTHER osascript spawn (the same process-spawn cost the fingerprint fix removed), and the existing mac foreground_window already pays one osascript at start (paste.rs:143) — adding a second at deliver is acceptable only because deliver is already async/post-transcription, NOT on the hotkey->beep path. Do not capture identity at start_recording.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Separate Windows (QueryFullProcessImageNameW on HWND) and macOS (PID->app name via osascript/System Events) implementations behind a shared get_target_app(); both have precedent in paste.rs's per-OS modules. Windows path is a cheap Win32 call; macOS path costs an extra osascript process — keep it at deliver time only so it never reintroduces hotpath latency.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Real and feasible, kept low/medium. ADJUSTED two things: (1) the finding says start_recording 'already captures the process id' — true on macOS (paste.rs:142) but NOT on Windows, where only the HWND is persisted (paste.rs:28-30) and the PID is transient inside the integrity check; corrected in detail. (2) Sharpened the dual-platform note: the macOS app-NAME path needs an extra osascript spawn — exactly the cost class the recent fingerprint fix targeted — so it must stay at deliver time, never at start. Down-weighted nothing; severity low is right.

verified_findings.title: No real VAD/silence trimming — leading/trailing silence is sent to the model and inflates latency
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/audio.rs:173-196 (has_speech is a boolean RMS flag, no trimming); src-tauri/src/whisper.rs:497-504 (whisper-server -sns flag only)
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED: the recorder computes per-buffer RMS and sets a single has_speech boolean when rms>0.001 (audio.rs:193-195) but never trims — the Stop handler writes the FULL resampled buffer to WAV (audio.rs:288-321) including pre-speech and trailing silence. whisper-server gets -sns (whisper.rs:503) which suppresses non-speech TOKENS in output, not silence in the input audio. Trailing silence is a known whisper hallucination trigger, and text_cleanup.rs:40-53 exists precisely to scrub 'thank you for watching'-class artifacts — confirming the finding's causal link. Trimming at capture is a real, cheap latency+accuracy win.
verified_findings.recommendation: In the Stop handler, before resampling (audio.rs:298), trim leading/trailing samples below an energy threshold with a short pre/post margin, reusing per-buffer RMS semantics already computed. Optionally add an energy-gate to drop long internal silences. Keep a generous margin so word onsets aren't clipped. Measure the 0.5s 'too short' guard (Dashboard.jsx:195) AND has_speech AFTER trim so a clip that is mostly silence doesn't slip through or get over-trimmed below the floor.
verified_findings.impact: Lower per-dictation latency (less audio to decode) and fewer hallucinated endings to scrub; compounds with the GPU/Metal work.
verified_findings.risk: Over-aggressive trimming clips soft onsets — conservative threshold + pre/post margin + a unit test on quiet speech. ORDERING catch: duration_seconds (audio.rs:304) and the frontend's <0.5s 'too short' check (Dashboard.jsx:195) are both computed from the buffer; if trimming changes length, both must be recomputed post-trim or a normal short sentence could be wrongly rejected. has_speech is computed live during capture (audio.rs:195) and would remain valid, but the trimmed-empty case (all-silence) must still report has_speech=false.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Operates on captured PCM in audio.rs — fully platform-agnostic; runs identically on Windows and macOS regardless of compute backend. Especially valuable on macOS where finding 2 means CPU-only decode, so every trimmed second saved is felt more.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed: no trimming, full buffer written, -sns is output-token suppression not input trimming, and the hallucination-scrub list at text_cleanup.rs:40-53 corroborates the trailing-silence rationale. Kept low/small. I add the ordering guard (recompute duration and the <0.5s gate post-trim) the finding only half-noted; without it a trimmed clip could be misjudged 'too short.' Verdict unchanged.

summary: Verified all 8 findings against the actual code, CI workflow, prepare scripts, and docs. The technical claims are accurate across the board — file/line citations check out, the asymmetric integrity posture is real (updater.rs SHA-verifies the installer at lines 110-123; packs.rs download_to and main.rs download_model_file have only size floors), only build-macos.yml exists (aarch64-only), and the Windows payload is hand-copied from %APPDATA% (prepare-resources.ps1:19,28). Confirmed 6 findings, ADJUSTED 2. Finding 2 (installer-hash CRITICAL): the specific 'live instance' it cites (stale 576c16d0 hash + never-created NEXT_PUBLIC var) was ALREADY RESOLVED per docs/2026-06-13-legal-audit-handoff.md:41 and the research session log (both env vars set to the verified hash, consistent across all four surfaces) — but the STRUCTURAL multi-copy drift problem and the server-supplied-hash-with-no-pinned-key weakness remain real and recurring; kept at high with corrected framing. Finding 5 (Intel Mac) is STRENGTHENED by a stale session log (2026-06-11-overnight-terminal1-session-log.md:35,49) that falsely claims the workflow builds both arm64 and x86_64 — the live workflow does not, so the gap is real AND mis-documented. Dependencies for the recommendations exist (ed25519-dalek, sha2, zip, ureq all present; semver and tauri-plugin-updater are not). No dual-platform regressions identified in the proposed fixes; the hashing/verification code is platform-agnostic and the macOS signing gap (finding 3) is the canonical asymmetry. I did not confirm severities beyond what the code supports — finding 3's macOS Gatekeeper 'hard fail not warning' claim is the one I'd most want runtime-verified, but it is plausible and correctly flagged as the largest undocumented gap.

verified_findings.title: GPU pack and HuggingFace model downloads have NO cryptographic integrity check — only a size floor
verified_findings.detail: Verified exactly as described. updater.rs:104-123 SHA-256-verifies the installer against a server-supplied hash, but the other two binary-download paths do NOT. packs.rs download_to() checks only `downloaded < min_bytes` (line 536, 50 MB CUDA / 5 MB Vulkan per min_bytes() at 87-92) and `downloaded != Content-Length` (lines 540-545), then extract_zip + run_install renames into models/ and calls state.whisper.reload() which spawns the contained whisper-server executable. main.rs download_model_file() accepts any payload >= 50 MB (lines 645-648) from huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp (line 605) and renames into models/. The CUDA/Vulkan packs are native executables launched as the speech engine. GPU-PACKS.md:53 confirms the publishing side ('publish its SHA-256 in the release notes and SHA256SUMS.txt') exists but the app never consumes it. ed25519-dalek + sha2 are already Cargo deps, so the streaming-hash block from updater.rs is directly reusable.
verified_findings.recommendation: Extend the version/download API to return a sha256 for each GPU pack and downloadable model; reuse the streaming-hash verification block (updater.rs:110-123) in packs.rs download_to() (BEFORE extract_zip at packs.rs:386) and in main.rs download_model_file() (BEFORE the rename at main.rs:650). Add pinned known-good pack hashes as per-PackKind constants as a defense-in-depth fallback so verification survives an API omission. The zip-slip guard at packs.rs:557 (enclosed_name) is good but does not defend against a wholesale malicious-but-valid zip.
verified_findings.impact: Closes a remote-code-execution vector on the two unverified binary-download paths (engine binaries launched with user privileges) and brings them to parity with the already-verified installer path. Affects every GPU-pack and multilingual-model install.
verified_findings.risk: Low — additive verification; main risk is a stale/missing API hash blocking a legitimate install, mitigated by the pinned-constant fallback. Note: the model path hashes a HuggingFace artifact the project does not control, so a pinned constant there would break whenever upstream re-publishes — prefer the API-supplied hash for the model and pinned constants only for the self-hosted GPU packs.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Both paths are cross-platform (ureq + sha2, no cfg gates in download_to/download_model_file). CUDA pack is Windows-only, but the model download and Vulkan path run on both; macOS gets the fix for free since the hashing code is platform-agnostic.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Code verified line-for-line; the asymmetry is exactly as claimed and the RCE framing is fair given the downloaded artifacts are executed as the engine. The legal-protection plan (docs/superpowers/plans/...:25) already noted these paths 'phone out' but only as a privacy/claims matter, not the integrity gap — so this is a genuinely new, code-grounded finding, not a re-discovery. One correctness nuance I added to risk: the pinned-hash fallback is only sound for the self-hosted packs, not the upstream HF model, which the recommendation should not pin.

verified_findings.title: Installer-hash mismatch: updater trusts a server-supplied SHA with no signing key, and the hash is hand-synced across multiple places in 2 repos
verified_findings.detail: The structural claim is verified. updater.rs:37-42 fetches {downloadUrl, sha256} from /api/echo/version and verifies the download against THAT server-supplied sha256 (updater.rs:104-123) — same-origin file and expected-hash with no app-pinned public key, so it catches transport corruption only, not a compromised/misconfigured origin. The hash is hand-maintained across multiple copies: the site env vars ECHO_INSTALLER_SHA256 + NEXT_PUBLIC_ECHO_INSTALLER_SHA256, SHA256SUMS.txt uploaded by scripts/release-checksums.ps1:5-7, and the value pasted into GitHub release notes (GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md:34 shows a hand-typed '3ba5081b…'). On drift, updater.rs:120-122 hard-fails 'Download integrity check failed' and deletes the installer (self-inflicted outage). GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md:89 still says 'No auto-updater' while updater.rs ships one — the runbook omits the hash-sync step. CORRECTION to the original finding: the specific live instance it cited (site served stale 576c16d0… + a never-created NEXT_PUBLIC var, page showed 'pending') was ALREADY RESOLVED — docs/2026-06-13-legal-audit-handoff.md:41 and docs/2026-06-12-legal-research-session-log.md:68 record both env vars set to the verified 6dbb09f5… and 'consistent across all four surfaces', and v1.2.3 was published with 74569fc6…. So this is not a currently-broken instance; it is a recurring structural fragility plus a real architectural weakness (no pinned signing key). The 'four places' framing is slightly off — there are effectively two site env vars + SHA256SUMS.txt + release notes; the count is illustrative, not exact.
verified_findings.recommendation: Two layers. (a) Single-source the hash: have release-checksums.ps1 (or a release script) emit the canonical sha256 and have the site API READ it from the uploaded SHA256SUMS.txt rather than separately-pasted env vars, eliminating the copy-drift. The standing rule already documented (V1.1-REBUILD-BATCH.md:60, GPU-PACKS-HANDOFF.md:145: update ECHO_DOWNLOAD_URL + ECHO_INSTALLER_SHA256 together) should be enforced by tooling, not discipline. (b) Move from server-supplied-hash to real artifact signing: adopt tauri-plugin-updater (documented as the second 1.x item, GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md:89-90) OR add a detached ed25519 signature over the installer verified against a const pubkey compiled into updater.rs (the app already depends on ed25519-dalek for activation). Update GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md:89 to reflect the updater now exists and add the hash-sync step to the runbook.
verified_findings.impact: Eliminates the recurring update-outage failure mode and upgrades update integrity from transport-only to origin-tamper-resistant. This is one of the two tracked open CRITICALs (the 'installer-hash mismatch').
verified_findings.risk: Medium — switching to a signed updater changes the release process and requires key management; the single-source-hash change alone is low risk and removes most of the recurring breakage.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: current_platform() (updater.rs:8-10) branches mac/windows and the verify code is shared, so a signing scheme applies uniformly. Critical asymmetry confirmed in code: the mac path (updater.rs:131-150) only `open`s the DMG and does NOT exit (user drag-installs), while Windows (updater.rs:153-160) spawns the exe and process::exit(0). A signing scheme must cover BOTH artifact types (DMG + NSIS exe), and tauri-plugin-updater's standard exe/dmg replacement flow differs from this custom mac drag-install UX — adopting it would change the mac update experience, which the recommendation should call out.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Real and severity-appropriate, but I corrected two things the original overstated: (1) the 'live instance' of breakage is already fixed per the handoffs, so this is a recurring/structural risk, not an active outage — framing changed accordingly; (2) the precise count of hash copies ('4 places') is loose. The core technical critique (server-supplied hash with no pinned key = transport-integrity-only) is correct and is the substantive issue. I also flagged that the mac custom drag-install flow means tauri-plugin-updater is not a drop-in — a feasibility nuance the original recommendation glossed.

verified_findings.title: Binaries are completely unsigned/unnotarized on both platforms; macOS will be Gatekeeper-blocked, not just warned
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:48-60 (windows.certificateThumbprint:null, empty timestampUrl, macOS block has only minimumSystemVersion); .github/workflows/build-macos.yml:54 (TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:"")
verified_findings.detail: Verified. tauri.conf.json:49-51: certificateThumbprint null, timestampUrl empty, digestAlgorithm sha256 (inert without a cert). The macOS block (lines 58-60) contains ONLY minimumSystemVersion 10.15 — no signingIdentity, no entitlements, no provider. build-macos.yml:54 sets TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:"" which is the Tauri UPDATER key, NOT an Apple Developer ID codesign identity, and there is no codesign / notarytool / stapler step anywhere in the workflow. Windows unsigned posture is an explicit owner decision (GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md:30-33,80; GO-LIVE-HANDOFF.md:39,50) mitigated by published checksums. The macOS gap is undocumented as a launch blocker. The claim that modern Gatekeeper refuses to launch an unsigned, un-notarized, internet-downloaded .app (rather than merely warning) is consistent with current macOS behavior, though I did not runtime-verify it on a specific OS version.
verified_findings.recommendation: Decide the macOS posture explicitly the way Windows was decided. Minimum viable: enroll in the Apple Developer Program, add codesign (Developer ID Application) + `xcrun notarytool submit` + `xcrun stapler staple` steps to build-macos.yml after `tauri build`, and set the macOS signing identity. If notarization is deferred, add explicit mac install instructions (xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine, or a spctl override) to the success page / README mirroring the Windows SmartScreen instructions, otherwise mac first-run is a hard failure. For Windows, if signing stays off, at minimum set a timestampUrl so a future cert works.
verified_findings.impact: Without this, macOS users likely cannot launch the app after download; blocks the mac half of a dual-platform product. This is the canonical undocumented dual-platform packaging gap.
verified_findings.risk: Medium — Apple enrollment + notarization is a known multi-step process; mainly cost and credential management, low code risk.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: This IS the dual-platform packaging asymmetry: Windows posture decided + mitigated (checksums, honest SmartScreen copy), macOS posture silently absent. Both need an explicit signing/distribution decision before mac GA. Note the empty TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY also means the Tauri updater-signature path is unconfigured, reinforcing finding 2's no-pinned-key point.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Config and workflow verified exactly. The one claim I could not fully verify from the repo is the runtime severity of Gatekeeper ('hard block' vs 'warn + right-click-Open bypass'), which varies by macOS version and download method — but the conclusion (mac needs an explicit signing/quarantine decision before GA) holds regardless of which side of that line current macOS sits on, so high severity stands. The TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY-is-not-an-Apple-identity distinction is correct and is the subtle error a less careful reviewer would miss.

verified_findings.title: No Windows CI; the shipped Windows payload is hand-copied from a developer's machine (non-reproducible, unpinned)
verified_findings.detail: Verified. The only workflow is build-macos.yml — no Windows CI, no automated installer production, no automated checksum publishing for the primary platform. prepare-resources.ps1:19 stages the Windows engine by copying whisper-server.exe + DLLs from `$env:APPDATA\ALAN Echo\models\Release` (lines 26-29) — i.e., from whatever build is installed on the release engineer's box — and grabs VC++ CRT DLLs from the newest local Visual Studio redist (lines 32-39). No pinned whisper.cpp version, no checksum of the copied binary, source build not in repo. The mac script builds from source but clones whisper.cpp with `git clone --depth 1` + `git pull --ff-only` (prepare-resources-macos.sh:25,29) tracking upstream master unpinned, so mac builds are also non-reproducible.
verified_findings.recommendation: Add a build-windows.yml mirroring the mac workflow: build whisper.cpp (CPU) from a PINNED whisper.cpp commit/tag in CI, stage via a CI-friendly script (not from APPDATA), run `tauri build`, run release-checksums.ps1, upload artifacts. Pin whisper.cpp to an exact ref in BOTH prepare scripts (replace `git pull --ff-only` with `git checkout <pinned-sha>`). Record the pinned ref and CRT redist version in the repo. Long-term, build the bundled binaries in CI and check their SHA-256 into the repo for byte-verification.
verified_findings.impact: Restores reproducibility and supply-chain auditability for the primary platform, removes the 'works on the release engineer's machine' risk, and lets checksums be generated automatically (feeding the hash-mismatch fix).
verified_findings.risk: Medium — building whisper.cpp (+ CUDA) in CI is non-trivial (toolchain, possibly self-hosted runner for CUDA); the CPU-only Windows build is achievable on hosted runners. Note the GPU/CUDA packs are produced by a SEPARATE process (GPU-PACKS docs) not these prepare scripts, so the CI scope here is correctly the CPU retail payload only.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: macOS has CI but only aarch64 + unpinned source; Windows has none + machine-local payload. Both need pinned upstream refs; Windows additionally needs a workflow to even exist. The pinning fix is symmetric and low-risk on both.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Every claim verified against the scripts and workflow directory. The APPDATA-copy is real and genuinely the worst reproducibility offender. I did not downgrade severity: for a paid product whose primary platform's exact shipped engine bytes come from 'whatever was last built locally', high is right. Effort 'large' is fair given CUDA-in-CI complexity, though the recommendation correctly scopes the achievable first step to CPU-only hosted-runner CI.

verified_findings.title: macOS CI builds Apple-Silicon only — Intel Macs get no build despite minimumSystemVersion 10.15
verified_findings.detail: Verified and STRENGTHENED. build-macos.yml targets only aarch64-apple-darwin (line 24 toolchain target, line 52 `tauri build --target aarch64-apple-darwin`) and uploads/releases a single arm64 DMG (lines 60,73). tauri.conf.json:59 declares minimumSystemVersion 10.15 (Catalina), spanning many Intel Macs. There is no x86_64-apple-darwin job and no universal2 build, so an Intel-Mac user has no runnable artifact (a native arm64 binary does not run on Intel; Rosetta does not apply). ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE: a stale session log (docs/2026-06-11-overnight-terminal1-session-log.md:35,49) FALSELY claims the workflow 'Builds for arm64 (Apple Silicon) and x86_64 (Intel Mac)' and 'CI workflow builds both architectures separately' — the live workflow does not, so the gap is both real and mis-documented, increasing the chance it ships unnoticed.
verified_findings.recommendation: Pick one explicitly: (a) build universal2 (`tauri build --target universal-apple-darwin`, requires both Rust targets + a universal whisper-server, which the prepare-resources-macos.sh build does NOT currently produce — it builds a single-arch binary, so the bundled engine would also need lipo'ing); (b) add a separate x86_64-apple-darwin job and ship two DMGs; or (c) consciously drop Intel and raise minimumSystemVersion / state 'Apple Silicon only' on the download page. Also delete/correct the stale dual-arch claim in 2026-06-11-overnight-terminal1-session-log.md.
verified_findings.impact: Determines whether Intel-Mac customers (a meaningful 10.15+ installed base) can run the product at all.
verified_findings.risk: Low for the CI target change, but the original understated one thing: a universal app needs a universal BUNDLED whisper-server too, and prepare-resources-macos.sh builds only the host arch — so option (a) is not purely a one-line target flag; the engine build must also produce both slices. Option (c) is genuinely trivial.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Pure macOS-arch concern; Windows ships x64 only (build-output.log:37 'Target: x64'), which is acceptable (Windows-on-ARM runs x64 under emulation). The asymmetry is that mac has two native arches and only one is built — and the bundled non-Rust engine binary, not just the Rust app, must cover both for a universal build.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed real and even better-evidenced than stated (the stale doc claiming both arches are built is a trap). I adjusted the recommendation/risk because the original called universal2 'a one-line target change plus adding the x86_64 Rust target' — that is incomplete: the bundled whisper-server.cpp binary is built single-arch by prepare-resources-macos.sh, so a true universal app requires producing/lipo'ing both engine slices, not just the Rust target. Severity medium is right — it blocks a user class but is a known, bounded packaging decision.

verified_findings.title: Updater download holds the entire installer in a single non-resumable stream with a hard 300s overall timeout and no completeness check
verified_findings.detail: Verified. updater.rs:72-75 uses a single `ureq::get().timeout(Duration::from_secs(300))` — an OVERALL cap, contrasted in-code with packs.rs:490-495 which deliberately uses AgentBuilder with timeout_connect(15) + per-read timeout_read(60) and the explicit comment 'Per-read timeout, NOT overall — a slow link is legitimate.' So a user on a slow link downloading a ~130 MB installer can be cut off mid-transfer for being slow, with no resume (whole download restarts). updater.rs reads content-length (lines 77-80) but never asserts `downloaded == total_size` before hashing — unlike packs.rs:540-545 which returns 'The download ended early' — so a truncated-but-stopped stream proceeds to hashing and fails with the confusing 'Download integrity check failed' (updater.rs:122) rather than a clear truncation error.
verified_findings.recommendation: Mirror the packs.rs download agent: AgentBuilder with timeout_connect + per-read timeout_read instead of the single .timeout(300). Add the `downloaded == total_size` completeness check (the content-length is already read at updater.rs:77-80) so truncation reports 'download ended early' before hashing. Optionally add HTTP Range resume for the installer since it is the largest single download.
verified_findings.impact: Improves update reliability on slow/flaky links and gives accurate error messages, reducing 'update failed' support load.
verified_findings.risk: Low — reuses an already-proven pattern from packs.rs (download_to).
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: The download/timeout code (updater.rs:72-101) is outside cfg gates and shared, so the fix improves Windows (.exe) and macOS (.dmg) downloads equally.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified by direct contrast with packs.rs in the same repo, which makes the fix unambiguous — the project already has the correct pattern and the updater simply didn't adopt it. Medium severity is fair: it only bites on slow/flaky links but those are exactly where an in-app updater earns its keep. Resume is correctly listed as optional, not required, since the per-read timeout alone removes the false-kill on slow-but-progressing transfers.

verified_findings.title: version_gt does naive numeric compare — silently drops non-numeric segments (prerelease/build-metadata mishandled)
verified_findings.detail: Verified. version_gt parses each dot-segment with `filter_map(|p| p.trim().parse::<u32>().ok())` (updater.rs:163-166), silently DROPPING non-numeric segments. So '1.2.3-beta' parses as [1,2,3] (identical to '1.2.3'), and '1.2.3a' parses as [1,2] losing the patch. A prerelease would never be offered as newer than its release nor vice-versa. The current app version is plain '1.2.3' (tauri.conf.json:4) sourced from app.config().version (main.rs:669), so this is LATENT today but a footgun the moment any prerelease/hotfix-letter/build-metadata scheme is introduced. semver is NOT currently a Cargo dependency.
verified_findings.recommendation: Adopt the semver crate for comparison, or at minimum strip and compare a prerelease suffix per semver rules (a version WITH a prerelease tag sorts BELOW the same version without). Add unit tests: 1.2.3 vs 1.2.3-beta, 1.10.0 vs 1.9.0, 1.2.3a trailing-segment cases. The crate is small and the app already pulls many deps.
verified_findings.impact: Prevents silent update-offer failures once any non-pure-numeric versioning is adopted; currently latent.
verified_findings.risk: Low — isolated pure function; easy to TDD.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent; affects update offers identically on Windows and macOS.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Logic verified exactly. Correctly self-classified as latent/low — the shipped versioning is pure-numeric so there is no live bug, only a trap for the future. I confirmed semver is not yet a dep, so 'trivial' effort is honest (add one small crate + a few tests). Worth keeping precisely because the project DOES contemplate prereleases (release-notes for v1.2.2/v1.2.3 exist and a v1.x roadmap is referenced).

verified_findings.title: Bundled engine and 148 MB model are read directly from the install dir / writable %APPDATA% with no integrity or version pinning at runtime
verified_findings.detail: Verified, including the precise candidate ordering. main.rs:808-810 sets data_dir = dirs::data_dir().join('ALAN Echo') = %APPDATA%\ALAN Echo (Roaming, user-writable). find_server_binary (whisper.rs:372-402) pushes the %APPDATA%/models candidates FIRST and the current_exe().parent() install-dir candidates LAST (lines 397-402), then `.find(|p| p.exists())` — so the writable %APPDATA% copy is preferred over the install-dir copy. With NSIS installMode 'currentUser' (tauri.conf.json:55) the install dir is also under the user profile. find_server_binary runs the first whisper-server it finds with no hash check.
