A local process with write access to the user profile (or a future pack-rollback path) could drop a substitute engine into a higher-priority candidate and have it executed. Lower severity because the attacker already needs user-level write access.
verified_findings.recommendation: Low priority given the local-write precondition. If hardened later: verify the bundled engine binary against an embedded hash before spawning, or prefer the read-only install-dir copy over the %APPDATA% copy when both exist (NOTE: this would invert the documented pack-override behavior where packs intentionally live in %APPDATA% and supersede the bundled CPU build — so it cannot be a blanket reorder; only the BUNDLED cpu binary lookup should prefer install-dir). At minimum document the trust boundary so finding 1's pack-verification fix is understood as the primary control on what lands in %APPDATA%.
verified_findings.impact: Defense-in-depth for local tampering of the executed engine; primarily relevant alongside the GPU-pack verification gap (finding 1).
verified_findings.risk: Low for documenting; MEDIUM for any reordering — the %APPDATA%-first ordering is load-bearing for the GPU-pack override mechanism (cuda_release/vulkan_release in %APPDATA% must beat the bundled CPU build), so naive 'prefer install-dir' would break GPU packs. Any fix must distinguish the bundled-CPU lookup from the pack lookups.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Search-path logic is shared (whisper.rs:369-419); only SERVER_BINARY_NAME is cfg-gated (whisper.rs:23-26). On macOS the signed .app bundle resource dir is read-only, so once mac signing lands (finding 3) this risk is lower there than on Windows' currentUser install — but %APPDATA%/packs are writable on both, so the pack path (finding 1) remains the real control on both platforms.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed the %APPDATA%-preferred-over-install-dir ordering claim by reading find_server_binary directly — it is accurate. Correctly self-rated low (requires pre-existing user-write access). I sharpened the recommendation/risk: the original's 'prefer the install-dir copy' would silently break the entire GPU-pack override design (packs live in %APPDATA% precisely to supersede the bundled build), so the fix is more constrained than stated. This is the right call to keep as documentation + a forward-looking note rather than an action item, with finding 1 as the actual control.

summary: I read every cited file (Dashboard.jsx, StatusPanel.jsx, main.jsx, UpdateBanner.jsx, Splash.jsx, DetailPanel.jsx, TranscriptCard.jsx, plus SettingsPanel/Onboarding poll sections) and cross-checked the backend (whisper.rs, updater.rs, audio.rs, main.rs transcribe/cancel paths, db.rs schema). The audit is mostly accurate and the strongest finding (#1, un-cancelable transcribe) is fully confirmed: there is no backend cancel/abort command, the dictate-cancel hotkey is unregistered during processing, StatusPanel's processing branch (lines 47-68) renders only an indeterminate bar with no controls, and whisper.transcribe() can block up to ~90s (plus a full restart+90s on a Failed engine). However several findings overstate the mechanism or miss existing mitigations: (#2) the double-stop_recording race is NOT reachable because applyStatus('processing') flips statusRef synchronously before any await and inflightRef is held across the await, and the backend already has a 310s hard buffer cap (audio.rs MAX_RECORD_SECONDS) — so I downgraded #2; (#3) the null-text crash is impossible because db.text is NOT NULL / Rust String (non-Option), and the 'two independent timeouts' framing is wrong since the shared effect clears its prior timeout — but the out-of-order/redundant-query parts are real, so adjusted; the EngineStatus exact-match (#9) and brittle string-coupling are confirmed. Net: 1 confirmed-high, several adjusted (real but mis-mechanized or partially pre-mitigated), none rejected outright except the specific unreachable sub-claims I corrected in place. No proposed fix endangers macOS or Windows specifically — all are shared React/ARIA changes or additive Tauri commands.

verified_findings.title: Transcribe ("processing") phase is completely un-cancelable and gives no progress — a slow whisper restart strands the user for up to ~90s (or ~180s on a failed-engine restart)
verified_findings.location: src/components/Dashboard.jsx:190-234 (handleToggle processing branch), handleCancel:236-242; src/components/StatusPanel.jsx:47-68 (processing view has no Cancel/Stop button); src-tauri/src/whisper.rs:302-335; src-tauri/src/main.rs:410-444 (transcribe command, no abort)
verified_findings.detail: Confirmed against code. After stop, handleToggle sets status='processing' (Dashboard.jsx:192) and awaits invoke('transcribe') (line 212) while inflightRef stays true (reset only in the outer finally, line 232). During that window: (1) StatusPanel's processing branch (StatusPanel.jsx:47-68) renders ONLY an indeterminate echo-bar animation — verified there is no Cancel/Stop button, no elapsed time, no copy beyond 'Transcribing...'; (2) handleCancel returns at the inflightRef guard (Dashboard.jsx:237) and additionally only acts when statusRef==='recording' (line 238); (3) the Escape handler calls handleCancel (line 252), so Esc is dead; (4) the dictate-cancel hotkey is unregistered during processing anyway (main.rs:291-294 only registers it for the recording duration). Backend: whisper.transcribe() (whisper.rs:303) calls wait_ready(90s), and on a Failed engine it restarts and wait_ready(90s) AGAIN (whisper.rs:310-318) — worst case ~180s, not just ~90s. The transcribe command (main.rs:413) runs on spawn_blocking so it doesn't block the Tauri runtime, but the frontend await is still fully blocking from the user's POV. There is no abort/cancel_transcribe command anywhere in src-tauri (grep confirmed).
verified_findings.recommendation: Add a Cancel control to StatusPanel's processing branch. Per-attempt token (useRef counter) captured before the transcribe await; Cancel increments the token and calls applyStatus('ready'); ignore the resolved result if the token changed. Add a 'Still working — large model can take a moment' caption after ~3s. Backend: add a cancel/timeout path (e.g. a shorter wait_ready and an abort command) so a hung whisper-server is recoverable. Note the worst case is ~180s (restart path), so a visible cancel matters more than the audit stated.
verified_findings.impact: Any user whose engine wasn't warm (cold start, model switch, GPU pack just installed, or a Failed engine triggering the restart path) hits a multi-second-to-multi-minute dead UI with no cancel; reads as a hang/crash.
verified_findings.risk: Low — additive UI plus a token guard; existing inflight serialization already prevents overlapping invokes.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Pure React + one optional Tauri command; identical on Windows and macOS. The restart path is engine-agnostic. No cfg/platform code involved in the fix.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Fully verified, including the negative (no abort command exists, processing branch has zero controls, Esc/cancel-hotkey both dead during processing). I strengthened it: the audit said ~90s but the Failed-engine restart-then-wait path (whisper.rs:310-318) doubles that to ~180s, making the missing cancel worse, not better. Severity high is correct; this is the top issue.

verified_findings.title: 5:00 auto-stop can silently no-op when a toggle is mid-flight; the double-stop_recording race is NOT reachable, and the backend already caps the buffer at 310s
verified_findings.location: src/components/Dashboard.jsx:155-159 (cap effect), handleToggle:175-192 (synchronous applyStatus+inflight), timer:139-152; src-tauri/src/audio.rs:13-15,174,197-200 (MAX_RECORD_SECONDS buffer cap)
verified_findings.detail: Partly real, partly wrong. REAL: the cap effect (Dashboard.jsx:156) calls handleToggleRef.current(), whose first line is the inflightRef guard (line 176); if a manual stop is mid-await at the instant elapsed hits 300, the auto-stop no-ops — but that's benign because a stop is already underway. NOT REAL (corrected): the audit claims 'two cap-effect runs can both pass the s===recording check before the first await resolves and both call stop_recording.' That cannot happen: handleToggle sets inflightRef.current=true synchronously (line 177) AND calls applyStatus('processing') (line 192) — which writes statusRef.current='processing' synchronously — BEFORE the await invoke('stop_recording') (line 194). So a second cap-effect tick is blocked by the inflight guard, and even if it weren't, statusRef is already 'processing'. ALSO MITIGATED: the backend has MAX_RECORD_SECONDS=310 (audio.rs:15); the capture callback stops extending the sample buffer past 310s (audio.rs:197-200), bounding memory even if the frontend cap fails — though it does NOT stop the session or notify the UI, so the on-screen clock could still run past 5:00 if the frontend cap genuinely failed.
verified_findings.recommendation: Lower-priority than stated. Optional: gate the cap behind a cappedRef so it fires once and is robust to the inflight no-op (reset when status leaves 'recording'). The stronger fix the audit suggested ('let the backend enforce the cap, frontend advisory') is only PARTIALLY pre-built: the backend caps the buffer but does not emit a stop event — implementing a true backend auto-stop would need a new emit('dictate-toggle')-equivalent, which is more than 'advisory.' Don't oversell the backend-cap recommendation as already-done.
verified_findings.impact: Edge case only: a manual-stop-at-4:59 collision makes the 5:00 auto-stop no-op (harmless, stop already happening). No redundant stop_recording, no wasted transcription via this path. Memory is already bounded by the backend.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Pure JS timing; identical on both OSes. The backend 310s buffer cap (audio.rs) is platform-agnostic cpal code.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Downgraded medium→low and rewrote the mechanism. The headline 'double-trigger / both call stop_recording' is unreachable because applyStatus flips statusRef synchronously pre-await and inflightRef is held across the await — I traced the exact ordering (lines 177,192,194). The only real residual is a benign no-op. I also found the audit missed the existing backend 310s buffer cap, which both blunts the memory concern AND makes its own 'have the backend enforce the cap' recommendation only half-true.

verified_findings.title: Search effect re-runs on every dictation (redundant query) and has an out-of-order result race; the null-text crash claim is impossible (db.text is NOT NULL)
verified_findings.location: src/components/Dashboard.jsx:261-272 (useEffect deps [query, transcripts]); fallback line 268; src-tauri/src/db.rs:12,40 (text: String / NOT NULL)
verified_findings.detail: Mixed. REAL: the effect deps are [query, transcripts] (Dashboard.jsx:272) because the catch-fallback (line 268) filters transcripts. After a dictation, handleToggle calls loadTranscripts() (line 216), replacing the array, re-triggering the effect and firing a fresh debounced invoke('search_transcripts') even though query text is unchanged — a redundant DB round-trip while a search is active. REAL: there is no request-id guard, so if search_transcripts resolves out of order, an older result can overwrite a newer one (setSearchResults line 266). NOT REAL (corrected): the audit says the fallback 't.text.toLowerCase()' will throw on null text. db.rs declares `text TEXT NOT NULL` (line 40) and the Rust struct field is `pub text: String` (line 12, non-Option), so the backend can never deliver null text — the crash is unreachable and the (t.text||'') guard addresses a phantom risk. PARTLY WRONG: the 'two independent 200ms timeouts scheduled by keystroke vs transcripts-change' framing is inaccurate — it's ONE effect; each re-run's cleanup clears the prior timeout (line 271), so at most one debounce is pending. The out-of-order risk comes from overlapping in-flight awaits, not overlapping timeouts.
verified_findings.recommendation: Remove `transcripts` from the dep array and read transcripts via a ref inside the catch (kills the redundant-on-dictation re-query). Add an incrementing request-id ref and ignore stale resolutions before setSearchResults (fixes the real out-of-order race). Skip the (t.text||'') guard — it guards an impossible state; keep code lean.
verified_findings.impact: A redundant search query fires on each new dictation while a search is active, and a slow search can be clobbered by a faster later one. No crash risk.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Identical on both platforms (SQLite FTS-backed search command, platform-agnostic).
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Downgraded medium→low and corrected two sub-claims. Verified db.rs: text is NOT NULL + Rust String, so the 'throws on null text' scenario is impossible — the audit invented a risk the type system forbids. The 'two independent timeouts' mechanism is also wrong (shared effect clears its own timeout). The redundant-query and out-of-order-result concerns ARE real and worth the small fix, hence kept, not rejected.

verified_findings.title: UpdateBanner has no terminal success/done state and no recovery from launching/mac_drag_install/error — banner can sit with no dismiss
verified_findings.detail: Confirmed. The Download button AND the Dismiss (×) button are both wrapped in `{!stage && (...)}` (UpdateBanner.jsx:47-87). setDismissed(true) is only reachable from that block (line 73), and the component returns null only when dismissed (line 25). Once stage is set to anything (downloading/verifying/launching/mac_drag_install/error), there is no path to dismiss: the error branch (lines 123-127) and launching/mac_drag_install branches (111-121) render only a text span with zero controls. Backend confirms these are real stages: updater.rs emits verifying (109), launching (125), mac_drag_install (143, macOS-only terminal instruction). The download onClick (line 50-57) optimistically sets stage='downloading' and only flips to 'error' on the invoke promise rejecting — verifying/launching come solely from the event stream, so a backend death between emits freezes the banner with no controls. The tracked installer-hash-mismatch CRITICAL surfaces here as exactly this dead 'error' span (updater.rs:120-123 returns the integrity-check error, which arrives as the rejected invoke → setStage('error')).
verified_findings.recommendation: Always render the Dismiss (×) regardless of stage. On stage==='error' add a 'Retry' (re-invoke download_update) and a 'Download from site' link. Treat launching/mac_drag_install as terminal-but-dismissible. Consider a watchdog that flips a stuck 'downloading' (no progress event for N s) into error+retry. This directly supports the tracked hash-mismatch CRITICAL — verification failures land in the dead error state today.
verified_findings.impact: A failed or hash-mismatched update leaves a non-dismissible banner; the user can't retry or clear it without restarting the app.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Both platforms affected; mac_drag_install (updater.rs:130-150, cfg(target_os=macos)) is a macOS-only terminal state that is itself non-dismissible, so the missing dismiss hurts Mac users specifically. The fix (always-render ×) is shared JS and breaks neither platform.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified against both the JSX (both buttons gated on !stage) and updater.rs (the stages and the hash-failure error are real). The dual-platform note is accurate: mac_drag_install genuinely can't be dismissed on macOS. Medium is right — it's a wedge, not a crash, but it intersects the tracked hash-mismatch CRITICAL.

verified_findings.title: Status, toasts, and inline errors are not announced to assistive tech (no aria-live/role=alert); transcript list isn't a navigable listbox
verified_findings.location: src/components/Dashboard.jsx:359-368 (error div), 414-424 (toast); src/components/StatusPanel.jsx:11-96 (status region); src/components/TranscriptCard.jsx:34 (button-per-row); src/components/Dashboard.jsx:373-391 (plain-div list container)
verified_findings.detail: Confirmed. The error div (Dashboard.jsx:359-368), the toast (414-424), and all three StatusPanel states (recording/processing/ready) change purely visually with no aria-live region, role='status', or role='alert' — a screen-reader user gets no announcement that recording started, transcription is underway, it failed, or text was pasted/copied. The transcript list container is a plain div (Dashboard.jsx:373) mapping TranscriptCard <button>s (TranscriptCard.jsx:34) with no role='list'/'listbox', no roving tabindex, no aria-selected, so arrow-key list navigation and selection state are absent. Verified positives the audit credited are accurate (StatusPanel Kbd labels, the Btn component). For a dictation product whose core audience includes AT users, this is a genuine gap.
verified_findings.recommendation: Wrap StatusPanel status text + the error/toast in aria-live (polite for status/toast, assertive for error) or add role='status'/role='alert'. Give the list role='list' (cards role='listitem') or a full listbox/option pattern with aria-selected + arrow-key roving focus. Purely additive attributes; no layout change.
verified_findings.impact: Screen-reader and keyboard-only users can't perceive state transitions or efficiently browse transcripts.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: WebView a11y differs (Windows WebView2/Narrator vs macOS WKWebView/VoiceOver) so announcements should be tested on both, but the ARIA attributes themselves are shared code that can't break either platform.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified the absence of any aria-live/role on the error/toast/status nodes and the plain-div list container. Effort 'medium' is fair for the listbox roving-focus pattern (the aria-live part alone is trivial). I'd note this is the lowest-certainty severity (medium leans toward 'should-fix' not 'must'), but it's a legitimate, code-confirmed gap, not invented.

verified_findings.title: On backend delete failure the row is still removed from UI (desync); Delete uses native blocking confirm()
verified_findings.detail: Confirmed. handleDelete (Dashboard.jsx:289-296) awaits invoke('delete_transcript') inside try/catch that only console.errors on failure (line 291), then UNCONDITIONALLY runs setTranscripts(prev => prev.filter(...)) (line 292) and fires 'Transcript deleted' (line 295) regardless of whether the backend threw. If delete fails (locked DB / IO error), the UI claims success and removes the card, but the row survives in SQLite and reappears on the next loadTranscripts()/restart — the 'deleted item came back' bug. Separately DetailPanel.jsx:87 uses synchronous window.confirm(), which blocks the WebView UI thread and renders an OS-native dialog off-brand from the app design language.
verified_findings.recommendation: Move the local mutation + 'deleted' toast inside the success path; on catch, toast 'Delete failed' and leave the row. Replace confirm() with the in-app modal styling or the Tauri dialog plugin already imported for export (Dashboard.jsx:320 uses plugin:dialog|save), giving consistent, non-blocking behavior.
verified_findings.impact: Rare but trust-damaging: a 'deleted' transcript silently returns; native confirm jars the polished UI.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: confirm() styling/behavior differs between WebView2 and WKWebView; the Tauri dialog plugin (already a dependency, used for export) normalizes both — so the recommended fix is safe and consistent cross-platform.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified the unconditional setTranscripts/toast outside the catch and the synchronous confirm(). Low severity is right — it requires a DB error to trigger the desync, and the confirm() is cosmetic. The Tauri dialog plugin is indeed already used (export path), so the recommendation is feasible without a new dependency.

verified_findings.title: Splash progress bar is fabricated and the 90s engine wait shows the same 'Initializing…' caption throughout
verified_findings.detail: Confirmed. loadEngine (main.jsx:81) increments progress by 3% every 500ms capped at 92, unrelated to real load; it only jumps to 100 when get_engine_info reports ready or after ENGINE_WAIT_MS=90000 (line 13,68). Splash.jsx:47-49 hard-codes the caption 'Initializing speech engine...'; only modelLabel (Splash.jsx:50-52, fed from info.model_label at main.jsx:71) varies. On a cold CUDA/large-model start the bar sits at 92% with a static caption — reads as a freeze. The backend exposes a usable signal: whisper.rs:284 returns status 'loading model' for Status::Starting and 'ready' for Status::Ready, so a real-ish progress/caption is achievable. No 'taking longer' message and no skip affordance (the dashboard already tolerates a not-ready engine).
verified_findings.recommendation: Either drive the caption off the backend status ('loading model' → 'Loading the {model} model — first launch can take a moment') after ~8s, and/or add a 'Continue anyway' affordance after ~15s that jumps to phase 'ready' (the dashboard surfaces engine errors on first dictation). Cap the synthetic creep lower so 92% doesn't read as 'almost done' for up to 80s.
verified_findings.impact: First-run and post-update launches look frozen at 92%; raises perceived slowness/abandonment.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Cold model load is slower on CPU-only configs (common on CUDA-less Macs), so the stall is more pronounced on macOS — same code path; the fix (real caption/skip) is shared and platform-safe.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified the synthetic 3%/92% logic, the 90s wait, and the static Splash caption. Confirmed the backend already emits 'loading model'/'ready' (whisper.rs:284), so the 'drive it from a real signal' recommendation is feasible, not hand-waved. Low severity is correct — cosmetic/perceptual, no functional break.

verified_findings.title: Beep oscillator/gain nodes never disconnected, and AudioContext is never resumed — hotkey-triggered beeps can be silent until a window click
verified_findings.detail: Confirmed. playBeep (Dashboard.jsx:97-120) lazily creates one AudioContext (line 100), but per beep creates osc(+osc2)/gain(+gain2) nodes and never disconnects them after stop() — transient accumulation, GC'd eventually. More importantly there is no ctx.resume(): a WebView AudioContext can start 'suspended' until a user gesture, and the very first beep is typically triggered by the GLOBAL HOTKEY with the Echo window unfocused (the whole point of the app), so osc.start() on a suspended context produces no sound and no error (the try/catch at 99/119 swallows nothing because start() doesn't throw). The start/stop beep is the primary 'recording is live' cue precisely when the user is looking at another app, so silent beeps until a first in-window click is a real feedback gap.
verified_findings.recommendation: At the top of playBeep: if (audioCtx.current.state === 'suspended') audioCtx.current.resume(). Set osc.onended = () => { osc.disconnect(); gain.disconnect() } (and for osc2/gain2). Resume/warm the context on first dictation. Verify the beep actually fires when triggered purely by the global hotkey with the window unfocused.
verified_findings.impact: The audible 'recording started/stopped' cue may be silent until a window click; minor node accumulation.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: WebView autoplay-gesture policy differs between WebView2 and WKWebView, so the suspended-context case may bite one engine harder — test the hotkey-triggered beep on both; the resume()+disconnect fix is shared and safe.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified: no resume(), no disconnect, try/catch can't catch a silent (non-throwing) start(). The suspended-context-on-hotkey scenario is plausible and the most user-visible part. Trivial effort is right. Note this is a 'likely' not 'proven on this machine' issue — whether the context is actually suspended depends on the specific WebView build — but the defensive resume() is correct regardless.

verified_findings.title: Engine warm-up polled redundantly by up to three uncoordinated loops (main.jsx + MicTest + StepTest + SettingsPanel)
verified_findings.detail: Confirmed. Four independent get_engine_info polling loops with divergent cadences/limits: main.jsx during splash (500ms up to 90s, line 82), SettingsPanel.startEnginePoll (800ms, line 64), MicTest (up to 60×500ms, line 837), Onboarding StepTest (up to 120×500ms, line 146). During first-run onboarding StepTest and the embedded MicTest can poll simultaneously. get_engine_info is cheap (whisper.rs:280 just locks and reads status), so runtime cost is minor, but it's the same uncoordinated-polling anti-pattern family as the fingerprint fix, with four copies of near-identical timeout/failed logic and divergent magic counts (60 vs 120 vs 90s vs 800ms) — a real maintenance hazard.
verified_findings.recommendation: Emit an engine-ready/engine-status event from the backend when whisper finishes loading and have a single useEngineReady hook/context subscribe once; components consume the cached value. If keeping polling, centralize cadence/timeout in one hook to kill the divergent magic counts.
verified_findings.impact: Minor redundant IPC plus four copies of readiness logic to keep in sync; low runtime cost, real tech-debt.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Backend event emit and the shared hook are platform-agnostic; no cfg code involved.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified all four poll sites and their differing limits. Severity low / category performance is fair — get_engine_info is genuinely cheap (a mutex read), so this is more tech-debt than a perf hotspot; I'd lean it's closer to tech-debt than 'performance', but the family-resemblance to the fingerprint anti-pattern justifies keeping it. Not a sibling of the hotkey→beep latency path though, so don't over-prioritize it.

verified_findings.title: Engine status detection is brittle string-matching (startsWith('failed'), exact === 'loading model') duplicated across files
verified_findings.location: src/main.jsx:73; src/components/SettingsPanel.jsx:63,82,486,842,850; src/components/Onboarding.jsx:151,162; backend strings in src-tauri/src/whisper.rs:282-288
verified_findings.detail: Confirmed. Readiness/failure is detected by string-matching a free-form status field in 8 places (grep-verified). EngineStatus (SettingsPanel.jsx:486) uses EXACT `engine?.status === 'loading model'` while every other site uses startsWith('failed') for failure. The backend (whisper.rs:282-288) currently returns exactly 'loading model' (Starting), 'ready' (Ready), 'failed: {e}' (Failed), 'idle', 'stopped' — so the exact match works TODAY, but any wording tweak (e.g. 'model loading') would silently break the SettingsPanel loading spinner while leaving the startsWith('failed') sites intact — inconsistent breakage. Fragile Rust-string ↔ JS-UI coupling with no shared contract.
verified_findings.recommendation: Have the backend return a structured enum/booleans ({ ready, state: 'loading'|'failed'|'ready'|'idle'|'stopped', detail }) — EngineInfo already has a ready bool (whisper.rs:297); add a machine state field and key UI off it, keeping the human string for display only. Centralize any residual parsing in one helper.
verified_findings.impact: Latent: a backend status-text tweak can desync loading/failed UI inconsistently across splash, settings, and onboarding.
verified_findings.risk: Low.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Shared code; no platform divergence.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified the exact-match vs startsWith inconsistency and that the backend currently produces the exact strings both expect (so nothing is broken right now — this is latent, hence low). EngineInfo already carries a `ready` bool, so adding a structured `state` enum is a small, safe change. Accurate finding; severity low is right since it's a future-breakage risk, not a current bug.

summary: Verified all 4 findings against the actual code. Findings 1, 3, 4 are real and well-located; finding 2 is real but over-rated on severity. Finding 1 (macOS osascript spawn on the hotkey-to-beep path) is the strongest — a true sibling of the fingerprint fix, confirmed at high. Finding 2 (sync record commands) is genuine but its head-of-line-blocking impact is small for these serialized, user-initiated operations — adjusted medium->low. Finding 3 (stale paste target + fixed focus sleeps) is confirmed medium, with a caveat that the "re-check foreground at paste time" recommendation is subtly mis-framed (we deliberately refocus the target, so non-foreground is expected). Finding 4 (no restart governor on whisper engine) is confirmed medium; the "concurrent storm" angle is narrow (Dashboard serializes via inflightRef) but the unbounded per-dictation 90s-stall respawn is the real defect. Dual-platform checks pass: finding 1 fix is cfg(macos)-only, finding 3 poll fix is cfg(windows)-only, findings 2 and 4 are platform-agnostic.

verified_findings.title: macOS foreground_window spawns osascript on the hotkey-to-beep path, sibling of the fingerprint fix
verified_findings.detail: Verified. start_recording (main.rs:268) is a sync command whose first real step after the now-memoized require_license is paste::foreground_window() at main.rs:272. On macOS that function (paste.rs:143-149) runs Command::new("osascript") talking to System Events to get the frontmost process unix id, on EVERY dictation start, BEFORE recorder.start() returns. The frontend gates the start beep on the awaited invoke (Dashboard.jsx:182-185: await invoke('start_recording') then playBeep('start')), so the osascript spawn is directly on the perceived hotkey->beep latency path. This is the exact shape the fingerprint memoization removed (process spawn on the pre-beep path). Windows foreground_window (paste.rs:28-30) is a single GetForegroundWindow syscall — cheap, no change needed.
verified_findings.recommendation: On macOS read the frontmost PID in-process via NSWorkspace.sharedWorkspace.frontmostApplication.processIdentifier (objc2/cocoa, sub-ms, no subprocess), preserving the PID semantics paste_into and the own-process guard rely on. Alternatively beep optimistically on hotkey fire (frontend) or make start_recording async + spawn_blocking. Keep the Windows path unchanged.
verified_findings.impact: Every macOS dictation start pays an osascript/AppleScript process spawn (System Events round-trip) before the audible start cue; this can be 100ms-1s+, worse than the finding's lower bound on a cold AppleScript runtime.
verified_findings.risk: The captured value must stay a PID: paste_into matches by unix id (paste.rs:168) and deliver_text's macOS own-window guard compares against std::process::id() (main.rs:482). NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication.processIdentifier returns that same PID, so the contract holds. Accessibility-permission behavior must stay equivalent.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Fix is strictly cfg(target_os="macos"); Windows is already optimal (single syscall) and is untouched. No cross-platform regression risk.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Read both branches end to end. The beep-gating in Dashboard.jsx:182-185 and the call ordering in start_recording (osascript at 272 before recorder.start at 285) both check out — this is a genuine sibling of the fingerprint fix. I nudged the impact wording upward because an osascript->System Events round-trip can exceed the stated 80-300ms on a cold AppleScript runtime; severity high stands. The recommended NSWorkspace replacement preserves the PID contract that paste_into and the own-process guard depend on, so it is safe.

verified_findings.title: Sync start/stop/cancel_recording block a Tauri runtime worker for the mpsc round-trip and device open
verified_findings.detail: Verified mechanically: start_recording (268), stop_recording (306), cancel_recording (312) are all sync fns. start blocks on rx.recv (audio.rs:102) while the recorder thread opens the cpal device and calls stream.play (audio.rs:266-274); stop blocks on resample + WAV encode + finalize (audio.rs:298-339), which is pure CPU on whatever thread runs the command. The async house pattern (spawn_blocking) exists at main.rs:350 (test_microphone), 410 (transcribe), 548 (read_wav_base64). HOWEVER the practical head-of-line impact is small: these commands are serialized by the user's own dictation flow (Dashboard inflightRef at 165-177 prevents overlapping toggles), they are low-frequency and user-initiated, durations are tens of ms for typical short clips, and there is no evidence of concurrent command pressure that would starve the worker pool. The change is a clean defensive improvement, not a latency defect on the scale of the fingerprint or osascript spawns.
verified_findings.recommendation: Make these async and wrap the recorder round-trip (and stop's WAV encode) in tokio::task::spawn_blocking, cloning the Arc<AppState> as transcribe does (Arc::clone(state.inner())). Crucially preserve cancel-hotkey registration ordering (main.rs:293-295) and the unregister-before-stop ordering (307,313). Low priority; bundle with finding 1 if start_recording is already being made async.
verified_findings.impact: Marginally removes worker-thread occupancy during record start/stop; not user-perceptible in the common serialized single-user flow.
verified_findings.risk: Low; spawn_blocking is the established pattern. Must keep cancel-hotkey register/unregister ordering and the paste_target commit-after-success invariant (main.rs:289) intact when moving work off-thread.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Device-open latency exists on both WASAPI and CoreAudio; the fix is platform-agnostic and touches no cfg-gated code.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed the commands are sync and the spawn_blocking pattern is the house style. Downgraded medium->low: the 'head-of-line blocking on the worker pool' framing overstates real impact for these user-serialized, low-frequency operations (inflightRef already serializes toggles, and a single user has no competing command traffic to be blocked). It is correct and cheap to do, but it is hygiene, not a measurable latency win on the fingerprint-fix bar. Effort small is right.

verified_findings.title: Auto-paste captures target at record start but pastes late; fixed 120ms focus sleep is fragile and HWND may be stale
verified_findings.detail: Verified. The paste target (HWND on Windows, PID on macOS) is captured at record start (main.rs:272) and consumed in deliver_text after DB save (main.rs:432,452). Windows paste_into does SetForegroundWindow then a fixed thread::sleep(120ms) (paste.rs:103-104), one retry with another 120ms (106-112), then SendInput Ctrl+V; targets slower than 240ms to accept focus (Electron, RDP, heavily loaded apps) fail GetForegroundWindow==h and degrade to clipboard-only (returns Err -> deliver_text returns false). IsWindow (paste.rs:93) only guards window destruction, not the user navigating to a different document/window in the captured app during a long dictation, so text can land in the wrong place. macOS has the same stale-target shape with a baked delay 0.15 in the osascript (paste.rs:170).
verified_findings.recommendation: Windows: replace the two fixed 120ms sleeps with a poll of GetForegroundWindow every ~20ms up to ~300-400ms — succeed as soon as focus lands (faster common case, more headroom for slow targets). The stale-target / wrong-document concern is harder than 're-check foreground at paste time' implies: at paste time the target is legitimately NOT foreground (we are refocusing it), so the useful signal is window/document identity, not foreground status; treat any wrong-target mitigation as settings-gated and conservative, or scope this finding to the poll-timing fix only.
verified_findings.impact: Fewer spurious clipboard-only fallbacks on slow focus switches; the poll change is a safe net win. Wrong-target mitigation is lower-confidence and should be gated.
verified_findings.risk: The original 'fall back to clipboard-only if target no longer foreground' idea would mis-fire because non-foreground at paste time is the normal case; implementing it naively would break nearly all pastes. The poll-timing change alone is low risk.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: The poll fix is cfg(target_os="windows")-only and does not touch the macOS path (which bakes delay 0.15 into osascript). The stale-HWND/PID concern applies to both platforms but no shared code is modified by the Windows poll change, so macOS is unaffected.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Code matches the finding: capture at 272, late delivery via deliver_text, fixed 120ms+120ms Windows sleeps, IsWindow guards destruction only. I kept severity medium and the poll-timing recommendation (clearly correct), but sharpened the recommendation/risk: the finding's 're-check foreground at paste time and fall back to clipboard-only' is subtly wrong because we intentionally refocus a target that is non-foreground by design — applied literally it would suppress almost every paste. Scoping to the poll fix keeps this safe and dual-platform clean.

verified_findings.title: Engine restart-on-failure has no cap, backoff, or breaker; a broken engine makes every dictation a 90s kill+respawn
verified_findings.detail: Verified. Inner (whisper.rs:69-77) has no restart counter or last-restart timestamp — only a generation counter for init-thread cancellation. transcribe restarts once on wait_ready failure when status is Failed (310-318) and once on post_inference failure (323-334); each start() bumps generation, kills the child, picks a new free_port, and spawns a fresh init thread that waits up to STARTUP_TIMEOUT. With a genuinely broken engine (corrupt model, driver that crashes on inference) there is no memory of prior failures, so EVERY new dictation pays a fresh kill+respawn and up to a 90s wait_ready stall (transcribe.rs:303/317/331), with no fast sticky-fail and no backoff. I confirmed there is no existing governor (grep for count/backoff/breaker/last_ in whisper.rs found none).
verified_findings.recommendation: Add a windowed restart governor to Inner: last_restart: Instant and restart_count, cap to e.g. 3 within 5 minutes; once the cap is hit, return the sticky Failed status fast (skip the 90s wait) until the window elapses, with optional backoff. TDD: a fake post_inference that always crashes; assert the number of start() invocations is bounded across repeated transcribe() calls.
verified_findings.impact: Converts an unbounded sequence of 90s stalls (one per dictation against a permanently broken engine) into a fast, clear failure, restoring responsiveness after the first couple of recovery attempts.
verified_findings.risk: Must preserve the legitimate single-restart recovery from transient CUDA OOM / startup crash (the current 310-318 and 323-334 behavior); a 3-per-5-min window does that. Do not break the generation-based init-thread cancellation.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Engine lifecycle is identical on Windows and macOS. CUDA OOM recovery is Windows/NVIDIA-relevant; the corrupt-model respawn loop is identical on the macOS CPU/Vulkan build. The governor is platform-agnostic.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: The structural claim is correct — no restart counter/backoff in Inner, two unconditional one-shot restarts in transcribe, and a 90s wait_ready each time. I trimmed the 'respawn storm across concurrent transcribe calls racing the generation counter' emphasis: Dashboard serializes via inflightRef and only Dashboard+Onboarding invoke transcribe (SettingsPanel mic test uses test_microphone, not transcribe), so true concurrency is narrow (mainly a one-time onboarding flow overlapping a hotkey). The real, confirmed defect is the per-dictation unbounded 90s-stall respawn with no fast-fail; severity medium and the windowed-governor fix stand. Kept verdict=adjusted to reflect the narrowed concurrency framing.

summary: Verified all 10 findings against the actual source. The fingerprint fix is confirmed in place (OnceLock memoization in activation.rs:119-123 + startup warm at main.rs:816-823), so the proposed findings correctly target the *remaining* post-stop -> text-visible segment rather than re-litigating the beep path. 9 of 10 findings are real and well-located; I confirmed 7, adjusted 3 (severity/effort/recommendation corrections), and rejected 0 outright. The strongest finding (regex recompilation in text_cleanup.rs) is confirmed and actually understated in one respect: fix_acronyms is partially *redundant* with the existing ALWAYS_UPPERCASE word-loop already present in fix_capitalization (lines 244-256), so the cheap-path implementation pattern already exists in the same file. The get_audio_level dead-code finding is solid — I grepped the entire src/ tree and found ZERO JS callers, and StatusPanel uses a wall-clock prop, not a live meter. Key corrections: (1) the COUNT(*) finding is even safer to fix than stated because get_stats() runs its own COUNT anyway, so the page COUNT is doubly redundant on the post-dictation path; (2) the optimistic-insert half of finding #5 is more involved than 'small' because the transcribe result omits `timestamp` (TranscriptCard.formatTimestamp needs it); the Promise.all half is genuinely trivial; (3) the engine-ready event finding requires threading an AppHandle into WhisperEngine::start (called from main.rs setup, set_setting, and packs.rs x2) — feasible but the medium effort is justified. No dual-platform breakage in any recommendation: all are pure-Rust or pure-JS except the paste-poll (#9, Windows-only SetForegroundWindow) and the macOS osascript note, both correctly flagged. The resampler get_unchecked suggestion is the one place to caution: unsafe indexing must keep the existing `.min(len-1)` clamp semantics or risk a panic/UB on the last sample — the invariant-hoist is safe, get_unchecked needs a correctness proof.

verified_findings.title: clean() recompiles ~30 regexes on every transcription (fix_acronyms + aggressive passes)
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED. clean() runs inside the transcribe spawn_blocking the frontend awaits (main.rs:421). fix_acronyms() (line 259-266) calls Regex::new(format!(...)).unwrap() in a loop over ALWAYS_UPPERCASE — I counted exactly 49 entries (finding said 50, immaterial), so 49 fresh DFA compilations per standard/aggressive transcription. apply_informal_corrections (line 268-281) compiles 11 more, tighten_phrasing (line 283-299) 7 more: 49 at standard, 67 at aggressive, every call. The intended pattern (static Lazy<Vec<Regex>>) is right above at lines 45-59 (RE_HALLUCINATIONS) and lines 56-59. Verdict-relevant nuance I found: fix_acronyms is *partly redundant* — fix_capitalization (lines 244-256, run at line 80 AND again at line 97) already uppercases ALWAYS_UPPERCASE via split_whitespace + slice .contains(), a cheap O(words) pass. So the expensive regex loop largely re-does work the cheap loop already did.
verified_findings.recommendation: Precompile into static Lazy<Vec<(Regex,&str)>> exactly like RE_HALLUCINATIONS — lowest-risk, fully behavior-preserving. The HashSet/tokenization alternative for fix_acronyms is even more attractive than the finding states because fix_capitalization (lines 244-256) ALREADY implements that exact split_whitespace+set-membership acronym pass — fix_acronyms could be deleted entirely if fix_capitalization's coverage is verified equivalent (it strips a slightly different punctuation set: ".,!?;:\"'()" vs regex \b). Do TDD: keep basic_cleanup (expects "API") and levels_visibly_differ green first; add a perf-pin test on a 200-word string. Note tighten_phrasing's 7 patterns are word-boundary literal replacements that are pure static-Lazy candidates with zero behavior change.
verified_findings.impact: Removes 49-67 DFA compilations + their per-call allocations from every transcription's user-visible cleanup. Several ms to low-tens-of-ms depending on level and text length.
verified_findings.risk: Low for the static-Lazy refactor; medium for deleting fix_acronyms in favor of fix_capitalization's existing pass (must confirm identical punctuation/edge handling). Existing tests pin the contract.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent pure Rust regex/string work. Identical win on Windows and macOS.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Severity high is justified: it's a per-call expensive recompute on the exact latency-sensitive path the dimension cares about, and it's the closest sibling to the fingerprint fix. Effort 'small' is correct for the static-Lazy version. I am MORE confident after finding the redundancy with fix_capitalization's existing acronym pass — the cheap implementation already lives in this file, lowering implementation risk. Only caution: the regex form is case-insensitive whole-word (?i)\bword\b; the static-Lazy version must keep (?i) and \b to preserve behavior.

verified_findings.title: WAV is read from disk twice per transcription (bytes + duration header)
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED but severity overstated. transcribe() reads the full WAV at line 321 (std::fs::read), and at line 337 get_wav_duration() (line 658-672) re-opens the SAME file via hound::WavReader::open. Crucially, the duration is already known twice over: audio.rs:304 computes `resampled.len()/16000` and returns it as RecordingResult.duration_seconds, which the frontend receives (Dashboard.jsx:194) — but transcribe is invoked with only { wavPath } (Dashboard.jsx:212), so the value is dropped and re-derived from disk. The re-open is a header parse only (hound reads the RIFF header + computes len), not a full data read, so the cost is one file open + ~44-byte header parse, not a second full read of the audio bytes. Real but small.
verified_findings.recommendation: The self-contained fix is correct and lowest-risk: parse from the in-hand bytes — hound::WavReader::new(std::io::Cursor::new(&wav_bytes)) — eliminating the second filesystem open with no signature change. Threading duration through the IPC boundary is more churn (touches the transcribe command + Dashboard.jsx:212) for marginal extra benefit; prefer the Cursor approach. Note the WAV is fixed at 16kHz mono int16 (audio.rs:312-315), so get_wav_duration's /channels is always /1 — the in-memory parse yields the identical value.
verified_findings.impact: Eliminates one filesystem open + header parse per transcription. Genuinely on the critical path but small in absolute terms.
verified_findings.risk: Low. The Cursor-based parse is self-contained in whisper.rs and produces a bit-identical duration.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent. The double-open is marginally worse on Windows where Defender real-time scan can touch recording_*.wav on each open; on a warm page-cached file (the common case milliseconds after writing it) the OS likely serves the second open from cache on both OSes, further shrinking the real cost.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Downgraded medium->low. The finding's framing ('read from disk twice') slightly overstates it: the second open is a header parse, and the file was just written so it's almost certainly in the page cache — this is microseconds, not the 'tens-to-hundreds of ms' tier. Still a real, trivially-avoidable redundancy worth fixing via the Cursor route. The threading-through alternative is correct but not worth the cross-boundary churn the finding itself acknowledges.

verified_findings.title: Audio callback computes RMS level every frame for a get_audio_level command nothing calls
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/audio.rs:193-195, 220-222, 247-249 (rms compute + *rl.lock() per callback); command at main.rs:344-347
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED. Every cpal callback (all three sample-format arms: f32 lines 193-195, i16 lines 220-222, u16 lines 247-249) computes rms = sqrt(sum(s*s)/n) and writes it under a parking_lot mutex (*rl.lock() = rms). The value is surfaced only by RecorderHandle::current_level (audio.rs:120-127) -> get_audio_level command (main.rs:344-347). I grepped the entire src/ tree for get_audio_level|audio_level|getAudioLevel and found ZERO JS callers; the only other references are the command registration (main.rs:1121) and a doc checklist. StatusPanel.jsx confirms the recording UI uses the wall-clock `elapsed` prop (computed by the Dashboard setInterval), NOT a live meter. So the sqrt + Vec stat-pass + mutex write are dead work on the active recording path. The has_speech detection at line 195 genuinely needs a magnitude but can avoid the sqrt (compare sum-of-squares/n against threshold²) and the rms_level write.
verified_findings.recommendation: Option (a) delete is correct and confirmed safe — no external/JS caller exists. Remove RecCmd::Level, current_level, get_audio_level, the rms_level field, and the per-callback rms write; replace has_speech with a cheap branch: track whether any sample's square exceeds threshold² (or a running sum-of-squares compared once). Keep the existing has_speech semantics so stop_recording's 'No speech detected' guard (Dashboard.jsx:201) still fires correctly. Pin with a test feeding silence vs a tone.
verified_findings.impact: Removes a sqrt + full-buffer stat pass + mutex acquire from every audio callback during recording, reducing audio-thread CPU and lock contention with the Stop drain — lowers xrun risk on weak machines.
verified_findings.risk: Low for the delete (verified no caller). The only must-preserve invariant is has_speech detection, which the existing tests/flow exercise via the 'No speech detected' path.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent cpal callback. Equal benefit on Windows WASAPI and macOS CoreAudio; most valuable on low-core machines where the callback budget is tightest on either OS.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: I independently confirmed the zero-caller claim with a tree-wide grep and by reading StatusPanel (wall-clock, no meter). Severity medium is fair — it's real dead work in the hottest loop in the app (fires every few ms during recording), though it doesn't block the beep, hence not high. The finding correctly notes the mutex write also contends with the Stop handler's std::mem::take(&mut *samples.lock()). Solid.

verified_findings.title: O(n) linear resampler runs single-pass on the full clip synchronously inside Stop, before the WAV is written
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED. On Stop, when device_rate != 16000 (the common case — mics report 44.1/48k), resample() (line 354-365) allocates output_len Vec and per-output-sample does src->idx, two clamped indexes samples[idx.min(len-1)] and samples[(idx+1).min(len-1)], and a lerp. This runs at line 298-302 INSIDE RecCmd::Stop, on the recorder thread, while the frontend awaits stop_recording (Dashboard.jsx:194) — so the user's stop->processing transition blocks on it. For a 5-min 48k clip that's ~4.8M output iterations. The per-iteration samples.len()-1 / (idx+1).min(len-1) recompute is real redundant work. Linear interp without a pre-filter is also low-quality for downsampling, but that's accuracy not latency.
verified_findings.recommendation: Sub-fix (1) invariant hoist is the safe, recommended win: `let last = samples.len()-1;` outside the loop, index samples[idx.min(last)] / samples[(idx+1).min(last)]. CAUTION on the get_unchecked suggestion in the original — replacing the clamp with get_unchecked requires proving idx<=last AND idx+1<=last for ALL i in 0..output_len; with output_len = (len/ratio) as usize and ratio>1 (downsampling, the common case) the last src index can land within bounds, but for UPSAMPLING (ratio<1, e.g. a rare 8k mic) the relationship differs — keep the .min(last) clamp OR add an explicit assert, do not blindly get_unchecked or you trade a few ms for a panic/UB risk. Sub-fix (2) moving resample off the Stop thread into the transcribe spawn_blocking is medium-risk plumbing (the WAV is written in Stop today; you'd write raw f32+rate and resample later) — defer. The 'let whisper-server resample non-16k input' idea must be verified against the actual server build before relying on it; don't assume.
verified_findings.impact: Tens to low-hundreds of ms off stop->processing for multi-minute non-16k clips; the invariant hoist is a measurable constant-factor win on every real recording (16k fast-path at line 300 almost never triggers).
verified_findings.risk: Medium. Invariant-hoist sub-fix is low risk. get_unchecked and off-thread moves carry correctness/UB risk — gate behind TDD with a known input/output vector and exercise both down- and up-sampling ratios.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent. Affects both OSes equally; nearly all real mics report 44.1/48k on Windows WASAPI and macOS CoreAudio, so the 16k fast-path rarely fires on either.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Real and correctly located, but I tightened the recommendation: the original's get_unchecked-after-single-assert is unsafe-by-default advice that could regress to a panic/UB on edge ratios (upsampling, or len==0 — though raw.is_empty() is guarded at line 291). The invariant hoist alone captures most of the per-iteration win with zero risk. Effort medium is right because the meaningful latency win (off-thread move) is the medium part; the safe part is small. Severity medium holds — it only bites multi-minute clips, which are not the dominant dictation length.

verified_findings.title: Post-dictation refresh does two sequential IPC round-trips (loadTranscripts then loadStats) on the user-visible path
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED. After a successful transcribe, handleToggle awaits loadTranscripts() (line 216, a get_transcripts IPC fetching a full 100-row page via db.get_page) THEN awaits loadStats() (line 217, a separate get_stats IPC). Two independent reads serialized — a full extra IPC+SQLite round-trip between 'transcription done' and the new card flashing. The same await-then-await pattern repeats at handleDelete (line 291-294, though delete uses an optimistic local filter at 292 then awaits loadStats) and handleSaveEdit (line 301-303). get_transcripts re-fetches the entire first page just to surface one new row, and get_page additionally runs COUNT(*) (db.rs:108).
verified_findings.recommendation: Promise.all([loadTranscripts(), loadStats()]) is the trivially-safe win — apply at lines 216-217, 301-303, and the onboarding 408-409. The optimistic-insert variant is more involved than the finding implies: the transcribe result (main.rs:434-442) returns id/text/duration_seconds/word_count but NOT `timestamp`, which TranscriptCard.formatTimestamp consumes — an optimistic prepend would need to synthesize new Date().toISOString() and risks a brief mismatch with the server's RFC3339 micros timestamp (db.rs:97) until the background refresh reconciles. Ship Promise.all now; treat optimistic-insert as a separate, carefully-tested follow-up.
verified_findings.impact: Promise.all removes one serialized IPC+SQLite round-trip from perceived 'text appears' latency after every dictation. Optimistic insert would remove both but needs the timestamp caveat handled.
verified_findings.risk: Low for Promise.all (independent reads, no shared write). Medium for optimistic insert (timestamp synthesis + ordering/dedupe vs background refresh).
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent webview IPC + SQLite. Identical on both OSes.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed and correctly diagnosed. I split the effort honestly: the finding bundled a trivial fix (Promise.all) with a non-trivial one (optimistic insert) under 'small'. The optimistic path is NOT small because the transcribe payload lacks timestamp — I verified main.rs:434-442 returns no timestamp and TranscriptCard needs it. Promise.all stays small/low-risk and should ship; flagged the rest as follow-up. Severity medium holds for a once-per-dictation extra round-trip.

verified_findings.title: Transcript list renders all rows without virtualization; 'Load more' grows it unbounded
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED. displayList.map (line 374-376) renders one TranscriptCard <button> per transcript with no windowing inside an overflow:auto div (line 373). PAGE_SIZE=100 (line 41), loadMoreTranscripts (line 54-69) appends 100 at a time into a single growing array (line 62). TranscriptCard is NOT wrapped in React.memo (verified — it's a plain function export) and runs formatTimestamp on every render (TranscriptCard.jsx:52, which does parseTimestamp + multiple Date/toLocaleString calls, lines 9-23). Critically: the recording elapsed-timer setInterval (Dashboard.jsx:142) fires setElapsed every 250ms while recording -> Dashboard re-renders 4x/sec -> the entire unmemoized displayList re-renders 4x/sec during every recording. Toasts (line 280) and flashId (line 220) also trigger full-list re-renders. The selected lookup (line 275, displayList.find) re-walks on every render too.
verified_findings.recommendation: Two tiers. Cheap+safe first: wrap TranscriptCard in React.memo (props are id/primitives + onClick — to keep the memo effective, pass an id-bound stable callback rather than the inline () => setSelectedId(t.id) at line 375, or accept that onClick identity changes and memo on the other props still helps via a custom comparator). useMemo the selected lookup. This alone kills the 4x/sec full re-render during recording. Tier two: virtualization (react-window/virtua) — the fixed-ish card height makes it tractable, but it adds a dependency and must be scroll/keyboard/selection-tested on BOTH WebView2 and WKWebView. Don't add the dep without that testing.
verified_findings.impact: React.memo + useMemo eliminates re-rendering N cards 4x/sec during recording and on every toast/flash — the biggest practical win for the resident tray user with long history. Virtualization additionally bounds DOM size for power users.
verified_findings.risk: Low for React.memo + useMemo. Medium for virtualization (dependency + cross-WebView behavior verification).
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: WebView2 (Windows) and WKWebView (macOS) both pay layout/paint for thousands of mounted nodes; virtualization helps both. WebView2 is the heavier renderer — verify smooth scroll there specifically. The 250ms-tick full re-render hurts equally on both.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Verified TranscriptCard is unmemoized and that the 250ms recording timer forces a Dashboard render 4x/sec, which cascades to the whole list — this is the most defensible part of the finding and a clear sibling to 'redundant work on a hot path'. The note about inline onClick at line 375 defeating naive React.memo is a real subtlety the finding glosses; I called it out. Severity medium is right (perf, not correctness; bites heavy users). The cheap tier (memo) should ship before any virtualization dependency decision.

verified_findings.title: get_page issues a separate COUNT(*) on every page fetch including 'load more'
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/db.rs:107-125 (get_page runs SELECT COUNT(*) then the windowed SELECT)
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED, and the redundancy is worse than stated. get_page (db.rs:107) runs SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transcripts (line 108) before every windowed SELECT — on initial load AND each 'Load more'. The frontend's hasMore is derived purely from row count (Dashboard.jsx:49 and :63 use `length >= PAGE_SIZE`), so the returned total is computed and discarded. Additionally I found the post-dictation path ALSO calls loadStats -> get_stats (db.rs:166-172) which runs its OWN COUNT(*) — so after each dictation the app computes COUNT(*) twice (once in get_page for the total it ignores, once in get_stats for the displayed total). export() (db.rs:218) calls get_page(0, 999999), loading every row plus a COUNT for an export.
verified_findings.recommendation: Drop the COUNT(*) from get_page entirely (or compute it only for page 0 if any caller ever needs total). hasMore is already row-count-derived, and the authoritative displayed total comes from get_stats. Change get_page's return to drop the i64 total, or keep the signature and return 0/skip the query — verify no consumer reads result.total (the frontend doesn't). For export, page through or stream rather than (0, 999999) for very large histories, but that's separate and low priority.
verified_findings.impact: Removes an O(rows) COUNT scan from every initial load and every 'Load more'. Negligible for small DBs, real for the long-history resident user — and removes the double-COUNT on the post-dictation refresh path.
verified_findings.risk: Low — the frontend doesn't rely on get_page's total for hasMore. Grep consumers of the returned total before deleting the column from the tuple.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent SQLite. Identical on both OSes.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed and I strengthened it: the finding missed that get_stats already does its own COUNT(*), making get_page's COUNT doubly redundant on the exact post-dictation path. Severity low and effort trivial are both correct. The one diligence step before deleting: confirm the Rust callers of get_page (search, export) don't consume the total — search.rs maps it away with `.map(|(t,_)| t)`, so it's safe. Genuinely free latency.

verified_findings.title: Recorder level/is_recording use synchronous channel round-trips under a Mutex on the IPC thread
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/audio.rs:92-127 (send + rx.recv per call) and main.rs:276 (is_recording inside start_recording)
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED. Every is_recording()/current_level()/start()/stop() locks cmd_tx (audio.rs:93 send()), sends a RecCmd, then blocks on rx.recv() for the recorder thread to service it (lines 102, 108, 114, 122). start_recording (main.rs:276) calls is_recording() — a full channel round-trip — on the hotkey->record path before starting. Because the recorder thread services commands serially in one while-let loop (audio.rs:138), an is_recording probe issued while the thread is mid-Stop (draining samples, resampling per finding #4, writing the WAV) queues BEHIND that heavy work and stalls. is_recording and level are pure reads of state the audio thread owns (the `recording` bool at audio.rs:136, rms_level at 134).
verified_findings.recommendation: Expose `recording` as an AtomicBool and (if the level survives finding #3's deletion) the level as AtomicU32 bits, written by the recorder thread and read directly by the handle — bypassing the channel for read-only queries. Keep Start/Stop on the channel as the sequencing source of truth. Relaxed ordering is fine for a UI hint. NOTE: if finding #3 is implemented (delete level/get_audio_level), the level half of this finding evaporates and only the is_recording AtomicBool remains — sequence #3 first, then this becomes even smaller.
verified_findings.impact: Removes a channel round-trip from the hotkey->start path and prevents is_recording probes from stalling behind Stop's resample/write. Small but on the same path as the fingerprint fix.
verified_findings.risk: Low — an AtomicBool for recording state is simple; the subtlety is the Start/Stop commands must still be the authority on transitions (the atomic mirrors them). Keep the channel for actual start/stop.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent std::sync::atomic. Identical on both OSes.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Correctly identifies that the serial command loop means a read-only probe can block behind a heavy Stop — a real (if small) stall on the hotkey path. Severity low is right: it only bites when a probe races an in-flight Stop, which is uncommon. I added the sequencing note (#3 deletes the level half), making this even more of an afterthought once #3 lands. The AtomicBool change is safe as long as Start/Stop remain channel-driven and the atomic is just a mirror.

verified_findings.title: Auto-paste fixed 120ms sleeps and a 1500ms clipboard-restore thread add baseline latency to delivery
verified_findings.location: src-tauri/src/paste.rs:104,108 (120ms sleeps) and main.rs:497 (1500ms restore delay); macOS uses osascript with delay 0.15 at paste.rs:170
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED. paste_into (Windows) sleeps thread::sleep(120ms) after SetForegroundWindow (paste.rs:104), and another 120ms on the retry path (line 108) — so a successful first-try paste adds a fixed 120ms before Ctrl+V injection (240ms on retry), on top of focus-switch time, as the tail of the user-perceived stop->text latency. macOS deliver_text shells out to osascript (process spawn) with a hardcoded `delay 0.15` (paste.rs:170-171) — both a subprocess spawn AND a fixed 150ms. The 1500ms clipboard restore (main.rs:497) correctly runs on a detached thread (line 496) so it does NOT block delivery — confirmed it's a no-block note, not a latency bug.
verified_findings.recommendation: Windows: replace the fixed 120ms with a bounded poll — after SetForegroundWindow, loop checking GetForegroundWindow()==h every ~10-15ms up to a 120ms cap, inject as soon as focus lands. CRITICAL: preserve the existing 'never inject into the wrong window' guard (paste.rs:105-113) — the poll must still bail to the retry/error path if focus never lands, and must not inject while GetForegroundWindow() != h. macOS: the osascript subprocess spawn is the dominant cost; a native AX (AXUIElement/CGEvent) rewrite is the real fix but is a larger, separate effort — do not attempt to shave the AppleScript delay alone as the win is marginal vs the spawn. Keep the retry fallback intact on both.
verified_findings.impact: Windows: cuts common-case paste latency from a fixed 120ms toward actual focus-switch time (often 20-40ms). macOS: the subprocess spawn dominates; only a native rewrite meaningfully helps.
verified_findings.risk: Medium — focus timing is finicky; polling too aggressively risks injecting before the target's message queue is truly ready (lost Ctrl+V). The wrong-window guard at paste.rs:105-113 must stay intact and be tested across multiple target apps.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: DIVERGENT by design. Windows path is SetForegroundWindow + Sleep (the pollable part). macOS path is an osascript subprocess + AppleScript delay — heavier, and the poll-based fix does NOT transfer (you can't poll inside a spawned osascript cheaply). The macOS native-AX rewrite is correctly flagged as a separate later pass. Any change here must be implemented and tested independently per OS.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Accurately located and the dual-platform divergence is the key risk the finding correctly raises — the Windows poll fix is real but does not help macOS, and the two must be treated as separate changes. Severity low is right: 120ms is a small, capped tail on an action the user already perceives as 'done talking'. I confirmed the 1500ms restore is correctly off-thread (non-blocking) — the finding rightly classifies it as a note, not a bug. Effort small / risk medium is the right pairing given focus-timing fragility.

verified_findings.title: Engine readiness is discovered by frontend polling loops (500-800ms) rather than a backend event
verified_findings.location: src/main.jsx:66-87 (loadEngine 500ms poll), src/components/SettingsPanel.jsx:59-66 (800ms startEnginePoll), SettingsPanel.jsx:834-854 (MicTest 60x500ms poll)
verified_findings.detail: CONFIRMED. Three independent pollers call get_engine_info on intervals: main.jsx loadEngine polls every 500ms up to ENGINE_WAIT_MS (line 68-83), SettingsPanel.startEnginePoll every 800ms (line 59-66), and the MicTest check loop up to 60x at 500ms (line 834-852). Onboarding.jsx also polls (line 149-161 per earlier grep). Each poll is an IPC round-trip that locks the whisper Inner mutex (info() at whisper.rs:280-281). The readiness transition is known precisely inside the init thread (whisper.rs:208 sets Status::Ready); it could emit one event. Worst case the splash/first-dictation appears ready up to 500-800ms after the socket actually bound, because the UI only learns on the next tick. (Minor correction to the finding: the extra try_wait syscall it cites lives in is_ready() (whisper.rs:270-271), but these pollers call get_engine_info -> info(), which reads inner.status WITHOUT a try_wait — so the per-poll cost is the mutex lock + IPC, not a syscall. The try_wait-per-call cost is real but on the is_ready()/check_whisper_ready path, not these specific pollers.)
verified_findings.recommendation: Have the whisper init thread emit a Tauri event (engine-ready / engine-failed) on the Status::Ready/Failed transition (whisper.rs:208/221/227), mirroring packs.rs:150-153's app.emit pattern; frontends listen and keep a single short fallback poll for the 'already ready before listener attached' race. FEASIBILITY: this requires threading a tauri::AppHandle into WhisperEngine::start(), which is called from main.rs setup, set_setting (main.rs:117/122), and packs.rs (lines 408/485) — the engine struct currently holds no AppHandle. That plumbing is the bulk of the 'medium' effort and is the reason this isn't 'small'. The init thread already runs detached, so moving a cloned AppHandle into it is straightforward once start()'s signature carries it.
verified_findings.impact: Eliminates 3-4 concurrent polling loops and their per-tick mutex+IPC cost; tightens perceived readiness by up to ~500-800ms on first launch.
verified_findings.risk: Low-medium — must handle emit-before-listener (keep get_engine_info queryable as the fallback, which it already is). Threading AppHandle through 4 call sites is mechanical but touches several files.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent Tauri events + whisper-server lifecycle. Same benefit on both OSes; the cold model-load being waited on is slower on machines without the GPU pack regardless of OS.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Real and the medium effort is justified by the AppHandle plumbing I verified (engine holds no AppHandle today; start() is called from 4 sites). I corrected one technical detail: the finding attributes a per-poll child.try_wait() syscall to these pollers, but they call info() (no try_wait) — try_wait is in is_ready()/check_whisper_ready(), a different path. The polling-cost critique still stands (mutex + IPC per tick across 3-4 loops). Severity low is appropriate: it's a first-launch one-time UX tightening, not a steady-state hot path. Keeping the fallback poll is non-negotiable for the emit-before-listen race.

summary: I independently read every cited file (paste.rs, updater.rs, main.rs, activation.rs, whisper.rs, trial.rs, settings.rs, db.rs, text_cleanup.rs, license.rs, Dashboard.jsx). The audit is largely accurate and well-grounded. Confirmed 8 of 10 findings outright, adjusted 2 (the CSV finding overstates the escaping gap — quotes ARE doubled and newlines ARE stripped, so the only real residual is unquoted numeric fields that today cannot be malformed; the macOS osascript finding's "join in deliver_text" sub-recommendation needs a correctness caveat about WHERE capture happens). The standout real bug is finding 1: start_recording (main.rs:269-272) calls paste::foreground_window() synchronously BEFORE recorder.start() returns, and Dashboard.jsx awaits the invoke before playBeep('start') — on macOS foreground_window() spawns osascript (paste.rs:142-157), so every Mac dictation beep is delayed by a process spawn. This is the exact sibling of the just-fixed fingerprint bug and the highest-value item. Finding 2 (updater overall-vs-per-read timeout) is also real and trivially fixable against the proven packs.rs pattern, and on a read stall the partial installer is genuinely leaked (the early Err return at updater.rs:90 skips cleanup). The remaining findings are correct but genuinely low-severity hardening. No finding is dangerous to fix on either platform if the dual-platform caveats below are honored; finding 1 carries the most platform risk (it touches the macOS-specific capture path and must not regress the working osascript paste/refocus step).

verified_findings.title: macOS: osascript spawned synchronously on the hotkey→record→beep path (fingerprint-bug sibling)
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED. main.rs:269 require_license then line 272 `let target = paste::foreground_window();` runs BEFORE `state.recorder.start()` at line 285. Dashboard.jsx:183-184 awaits `invoke('start_recording')` then calls `playBeep('start')`, so the whole synchronous backend cost gates the beep. On macOS foreground_window() is `Command::new("osascript").args([...]).output()` (paste.rs:143-149) — a full process spawn + AppleScript/System Events round-trip, 100-300ms+ warm. On Windows it is a bare `GetForegroundWindow()` (paste.rs:28-30), ~microseconds — so the bug is macOS-only and would not surface on the Windows dev machine. This is structurally identical to the fingerprint perf bug the codebase just fixed.
verified_findings.recommendation: Replace the macOS CAPTURE with a non-subprocess API: NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication.processIdentifier via objc2/cocoa returns the frontmost PID synchronously and fast, no spawn. Keep the existing osascript paste_into for refocus+Cmd+V (it works and needs Accessibility regardless). IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the proposed alternate fix: if you keep osascript and move capture to a side thread, that thread must still START at record time (capture-at-start is the whole point — the target is the app focused when the hotkey fired, which differs from whatever is focused at paste time after the user may have clicked our window). 'Join only in deliver_text' is fine ONLY if the spawn happens in start_recording; do not defer the CAPTURE itself to paste time. Add a perf test mirroring activation.rs::machine_fingerprint_is_memoized asserting foreground_window() returns in <20ms.
verified_findings.impact: Every macOS dictation start beep is delayed by the osascript spawn (100-300ms+), making the hotkey feel laggy — the same regression class the fingerprint memoization just eliminated, on the other platform.
verified_findings.risk: Switching the capture off osascript risks Accessibility/permission and bundle-linking differences (objc2/cocoa adds a dependency). Mitigate by keeping osascript for paste-time refocus and only replacing the capture call; gate behind a manual macOS smoke test since the resident-app/dev-build constraint blocks `tauri dev` GUI testing.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: macOS-only latency bug; Windows path (GetForegroundWindow, paste.rs:28-30) is already fast and MUST NOT be regressed. The fix is macOS-side only and must preserve the existing osascript-based paste_into refocus+keystroke step.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Kept at high — the latency, platform-asymmetry, and beep-gating chain are all verified in code, and it is the textbook sibling of the accepted fingerprint fix. Adjusted the recommendation: the 'capture on a side thread, join in deliver_text' wording could be misread as capturing at paste time, which would capture the WRONG window (our own UI). Capture must occur at record start; only the JOIN may be deferred. Effort stays medium because the clean fix (NSWorkspace) pulls in objc2/cocoa bindings and needs a macOS-only manual verification the resident-app constraint complicates.

verified_findings.title: Updater download has no per-read timeout — a stalled connection hangs the update thread up to 300s
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED. updater.rs:72-73 is `ureq::get(download_url).timeout(Duration::from_secs(300))` — ureq's `.timeout()` is the overall request deadline, not a per-read idle timeout. The read loop at updater.rs:89-99 (`reader.read(&mut buf)`) can block on a stalled socket until the 300s overall budget elapses. By contrast packs.rs:489-495 (model pack) and main.rs:610-613 (multilingual model) both use `AgentBuilder::timeout_connect(15s).timeout_read(60s)`. Also verified the leaked-partial claim: on a read error, updater.rs:90 returns Err immediately and the function exits WITHOUT removing installer_path — cleanup (remove_file) only happens on the missing-hash branch (line 105) and the hash-mismatch branch (line 121), not on a read/write/flush error. So a stalled download both hangs AND leaks the half-written file.
verified_findings.recommendation: Replace the one-shot get with an AgentBuilder mirroring packs.rs: `.timeout_connect(15s).timeout_read(60s).build()` then `.get(url).call()`. Additionally, wrap the read loop so a read/write error also removes the partial installer before returning (mirror the existing remove_file cleanup), since the leaked partial is real on the error path.
verified_findings.impact: On a stalled network the update appears hung for up to 5 minutes with a frozen progress bar; users force-quit and a half-written ALAN-Echo-Update.exe/.dmg is left in the data dir (only removed on missing-hash or hash-mismatch, not on a read hang).
verified_findings.risk: None for the timeout change — strictly tightens behavior and matches the proven packs.rs/model-download pattern. The added partial-cleanup-on-error is also low risk.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Affects Windows (.exe) and macOS (.dmg) downloads identically; pure ureq config, no platform branches.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed at medium. The overall-vs-per-read timeout distinction is correct ureq semantics and the inconsistency with packs.rs/main.rs is real in the tree. I additionally verified (the finding asserted it) that the partial file genuinely leaks on the read-error path — line 90's early Err return bypasses every remove_file call — so the impact statement is accurate, not speculative.

verified_findings.title: check_for_update / download URL embeds raw license key in query string without URL-encoding
verified_findings.detail: VERIFIED. main.rs:675-678 interpolates the stored license_key directly into `https://.../api/echo/download?key={}`. license.rs CHARSET (b"ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789") is URL-safe, so a well-formed key is benign. The finding's key insight checks out: the corrupt-settings salvage path (main.rs:847-864) scrapes the raw value BETWEEN QUOTES out of the broken file and stores it verbatim — it does NOT run validate_key or the trim/uppercase/normalize that validate_license applies (main.rs:138). So a salvaged license_key can be arbitrary text, and the well-formed invariant is not guaranteed at this call site.
verified_findings.recommendation: Percent-encode the key when building the URL (urlencoding/form_urlencoded) AND validate it with LicenseManager::validate_key before use, returning an error / skipping the synthesized URL if it doesn't match the expected format. Cheap defense-in-depth; also a good place to normalize the salvaged key.
verified_findings.impact: Low today (charset URL-safe); guards against a malformed/salvaged key producing a broken update URL or, if the charset ever widened, query-injection into the download endpoint.
verified_findings.risk: None.
verified_findings.dual_platform_note: Platform-independent; identical URL construction on Windows and macOS.
verified_findings.skeptic_note: Confirmed at low. I specifically checked the load-bearing claim — that license_key isn't actually guaranteed well-formed — and the salvage path at main.rs:847-864 does store an unvalidated, unnormalized scraped substring, so the premise holds.
